trigger, inventory skew leaning against position, loss-triggered parameter recalibration (checks pnlSinceRecalib against a threshold, only resets params on breach, otherwise leaves them alone), timer-based requoting (250ms cycle) via addOrder/cancelOrder using PROTOCOL.md's request/reply format, and real fill processing (position/avgEntryPrice/realizedPnL) wired from E/T market data messages matched against own $SENDER\n- Added dedicated logging: FILL rows (one per own trade: side, price, volume, position before/after, pnlDelta, realizedPnL, pnlSinceRecalib) and periodic PNL snapshot rows (position, avgEntryPrice, realizedPnL, pnlSinceRecalib, rollingMean, rollingStd, zscore, ref_price, resting bid/ask) written into bbo_data.csv every requote cycle; also added a separate dedicated pnl.csv (via writePnlRow) that additionally computes unrealized PnL (marking open position against current mid) and total_pnl = realized + unrealized, since bbo_data.csv's PNL rows only have realized PnL and miss a bleeding open position\n- Ran a pilot and found negative PnL; investigated whether it's due to the missing hedger (concluded no \u2014 hedger controls risk/exposure duration, not quoting edge, so a missing hedger wouldn't itself cause negative realized PnL) and is now moving into building a proper EDA on the FILL/PNL/pnl.csv output to diagnose the actual cause (leading hypotheses: fair-value lag during the mover's price walks causing adverse selection, or the 250ms requote cadence being too slow relative to sweep events)\n- Initial EDA findings (small-subset sample, later superseded by a longer run): identified that the \"mover\" bot trades AAH6 very frequently (thousands of mover trades vs. single digits/low teens on AAM6/AAU6) and its trading is likely what drives price shifts in the other two instruments as well\n- Re-ran the full EDA (order posting, trade analysis, half-life, ACF, cointegration) after letting the sim run longer (~1157 return obs vs. ~467 originally, still under a full day): all three instruments now show statistically significant individual mean-reversion (half-lives ~16-36s, p-values 0.0005-0.026, versus insignificant p-values 0.17-0.28 in the small-sample run); Johansen test now shows full rank 3 (cointegrating relations at 95%) rather than rank 2 from the small-sample run, consistent with each individual series being near-stationary rather than needing cross-instrument combination to achieve stationarity; pairwise Engle-Granger cointegration still holds for all three pairs; ADF on the current (rank-3) Johansen first eigenvector confirms strong stationarity (statistic -8.0, p\u22480.0000); order-arrival ACF remains significant across nearly all lags 1-40 for all three instruments, treated as characteristic bursty/clustered order flow rather than a tradeable signal\n- Conclusion drawn from the updated EDA: cross-instrument hedging (via cointegration/Johansen weights) is not worth the added complexity given individual mean-reversion is now the dominant, well-supported finding; sticking with the original plan of independent per-instrument flattening in the hedger, and planning to note in NOTES.md that this choice is supported by the individual mean-reversion results reducing the marginal benefit of cross-instrument hedging\n- Next planned step for the hedger: use the mean-reversion half-lives (~16-36s) as justification for a more patient/passive hedging trigger and sizing approach (letting small residual positions ride briefly since they're statistically likely to shrink on their own) rather than aggressively crossing the spread immediately whenever off-flat\n- Found and read the actual \"mover\" bot simulation code: it only trades FRONT (AAH6), never AAM6/AAU6 directly; every 2.5-4.5s picks a new random target price (coin-flip direction, step size 20-60, or 40-120 on a ~30% \"shock\" chance) and every 0.2s walks price toward that target via a single marketable limit order sized to eat exactly the resting depth between current price and target plus a 20% buffer \u2014 so \"sweeps\" are not a separate behavior from \"walking,\" just the large-magnitude tail of the same mechanism; decided this should be built into the quoter (detecting in-progress mover walks / reacting to them) rather than treated as a separate task\n- Found a fair_value() reference implementation (likely the exchange's own fair-value/reference-price definition) using a microprice formula: falls back to simple mid when spread >= 2 ticks or when both book-side volumes are zero, otherwise computes (bid*ask_vol + ask*bid_vol)/(bid_vol+ask_vol) \u2014 decided to switch the quoter's fair value calc to this microprice approach (confirmed this snippet is from the actual simulation/exchange source, not just inspiration)\n- Found and read the taker's action logic: every 0.05-0.5s it reads BBO from one randomly chosen instrument but submits its order to an independently, separately randomly chosen instrument (two separate random.choice(ALL) calls, not tied together) \u2014 meaning taker orders are frequently priced using a different instrument's book than the one they're actually submitted to, a likely source of noisy/mispriced fills distinct from the mover's behavior; taker order price is aggressive/marketable (ask+0-6 ticks or bid-0-6 ticks) and size is skewed toward small values (1 + int(20*random()**2), squared-uniform distribution concentrates near small sizes)\n- Ran own-book microprice change and compared against previous rolling-mean baseline: AAH6 results are similar (fair-value estimation was never the dominant AAH6 problem \u2014 confirms the mover's walk mechanism, not stale pricing, is the main AAH6 loss driver); AAM6 results got worse than the rolling-mean baseline (confirms the piggyback hypothesis \u2014 AAM6/AAU6's own book is thin/noisy and disconnected from the price the dominant background quoters actually use, so an accurate own-book estimate is a confident estimate of the wrong thing)\n- Decided on the AAM6/AAU6 fix: regress each piggyback instrument on the driving instrument (AAM6 = intercept + hedge_ratio*AAH6 + residual, same direction as the true generative relationship AAM6 = AAH6 + rel found in the quoter source) and price off that regression instead of own-book microprice; will compute this as an incremental/rolling OLS in C++ (running sums n, \u03a3x, \u03a3y, \u03a3xy, \u03a3x\u00b2 updated per sample, O(1) per update) rather than in a separate Python process, both because strategy/ must not be Python per the task spec and because the incremental OLS is computationally trivial (cheaper than the existing rolling-mean/z-score logic already in C++)\n- Decided to keep own-book microprice as a cold-start fallback for the regression-based estimate, mirroring the existing rolling-mean \u2192 EX_META ref_price fallback pattern already in the quoter\n- Measured how long it takes to get enough samples for a statistically significant Engle-Granger p-value: captured ~816s (~13.6 min) of live session data, resampled to a 500ms cadence, yielding 1632 samples \u2014 this was the point p-values first became reliably significant (consistent with the earlier finding that small/underpowered samples gave misleadingly insignificant results); concluded the 500ms-spaced sampling cadence (not raw tick data, which is highly autocorrelated and would inflate sample count without adding independent information) is what makes the p-value trustworthy, so decided to sample into the regression's rolling buffer at a fixed ~500ms cadence rather than feeding every raw BBO tick, and to treat ~13-14 minutes as the expected cold-start duration before trusting the regression, falling back to own-book microprice until then\n- Plan to generalize driver detection beyond the known AAH6 case: regress instruments against each other to find which instrument (Y) reliably explains multiple others (X1, X2...); flagged that contemporaneous-only regression can't distinguish a true driver from a fellow piggybacker (since two piggybackers of the same driver will also correlate with each other), so lead-lag structure (checking whether Y_{t-1} predicts X_t about as well as Y_t does) may be needed to confirm direction if generalizing beyond the AAH6-known-driver case\n- Root cause for AAH6 losses identified as being run over by the mover repeatedly: loss-triggered recalibration was making this worse, not better, because recalibrating after a bad fill resets fair value toward the price the mover just imposed, then requoting there puts the quoter right back in the mover's path \u2014 decided this needs a dedicated walk-detection/defense mechanism rather than adjusting the recalibration loss threshold\n- Decided on a mover walk-detector for AAH6 based on consecutive same-side adverse fills in a short window (e.g. 2+ fills on the same side within one requote cycle) as the primary signal, since it directly mirrors the confirmed mechanism (mover eats resting depth on one side via rapid marketable orders); response on trigger is to cancel/pull the resting order on that side and pause repricing on that side for a cooldown period, rather than immediately recalibrating and requoting into the same path; considered book-imbalance-via-microprice-divergence and rate-of-BBO-change as secondary/refinement signals if time allows\n- Decided on a clean separation of responsibilities: the quoter only defends (pulls/pauses quotes when it detects it's being run over), and actual position flattening stays entirely the hedger's job \u2014 the quoter will not self-flatten by crossing the spread\n- Found and read the actual background quoter bot source for AAM6/AAU6: it computes `center = round(fair_value(AAH6) + rel)` each time fair_value(AAH6) changes, then requotes symmetrically around center (bid at center-offset-i, ask at center+offset+i per level) \u2014 rel is a fixed constant chosen once per contract at bot startup and never changes during the session\n- Decided to abandon the regression/cointegration approach for AAM6/AAU6 pricing in favor of directly recovering rel, since it's an exact deterministic constant (not a statistical relationship): rel = mid(AAM6_BBO) - fair_value(AAH6), observable almost immediately (a short robust sample, e.g. median over a small window, rather than the ~14min cointegration cold-start) rather than needing sustained data collection; plan to verify this against already-captured BBO CSV data before implementing\n- Settled offset-detection method for identifying driver vs piggyback instruments and recovering AAM6/AAU6 fair value: piggyback instruments should reliably regress onto the true driver instrument (used to ID which instrument is the driver when the number/identity of instruments in play isn't known in advance); once driver is identified, recover the background quoter bot's center per requote by taking (max_bid + min_ask)/2 across its innermost order levels immediately after detecting a requote burst \u2014 this cancels the bot's offset out algebraically regardless of its value, since orders sit symmetrically at center\u00b1offset\u00b1i; then rel = fair_value(driver) - center, and the quoter quotes a tick or two inside rel\u00b1offset to sit tighter than the background bots\n- Known risks/caveats on the offset-detection method, explicitly accepted: (1) requires being first to sample right after a requote burst \u2014 asymmetric fills on one side (e.g. from the mover hitting one side only) before sampling will bias the center estimate, though symmetric fills still cancel correctly; (2) works fine even if the market data feed is anonymized/lacks sender attribution, since it only needs aggregate BBO read right after a detected requote-burst event, not per-order attribution \u2014 but requires PROTOCOL.md to confirm individual order messages (A/C/E/T) arrive in a way that lets a requote burst be detected as a discrete event, not just a fully pre-aggregated BBO snapshot; (3) the whole approach assumes background quoters use this same fixed-rel deterministic quoting logic in the actual grading market, which is unverified and could be wrong, with no fast statistical fallback available if it is wrong (statistical/cointegration-based estimation takes too long, microprice/rolling-mean approach (accepting worse edge) rather than trusting a wrong deterministic assumption\n- Current status: microprice (own-book) implemented and tested; rel-based direct pricing `center = round(fair_value(AAH6) + rel)` each time fair_value(AAH6) changes, then requotes symmetrically around center (bid at center-offset-i, ask at center+offset+i per level) \u2014 rel is a fixed constant chosen once per contract at bot startup and never changes during the session\n- Decided to abandon the regression/cointegration approach for AAM6/AAU6 pricing in favor of directly recovering rel, since it's an exact deterministic constant (not a statistical relationship): rel = mid(AAM6_BBO) - fair_value(AAH6), observable almost immediately (a short robust sample, e.g. median over a small window, rather than the ~14min cointegration cold-start) rather than needing sustained data collection; plan to verify this against already-captured BBO CSV data before implementing\n- Settled which instrument is the driver when the number/identity of instruments in play isn't known in advance); once driver is identified, recover the background quoter bot's center per requote by taking (max_bid + min_ask)/2 across its innermost order levels immediately after detecting a requote burst \u2014 this cancels the bot's offset out algebraically regardless of its value, since orders sit symmetrically at center\u00b1offset\u00b1i; then rel = fair_value(driver) - center, and the quoter quotes a tick or two inside rel\u00b1offset to sit tighter than the background bots\n- Known side only) before sampling will bias the center estimate, though symmetric fills still cancel correctly; (2) works fine even if the market data feed is anonymized/lacks sender attribution, since it only needs aggregate BBO read right after a detected requote-burst event, not per-order attribution \u2014 but requires PROTOCOL.md to confirm individual order messages (A/C/E/T) arrive in a way that lets a requote burst be detected as a discrete event, not just a fully pre-aggregated BBO snapshot; (3) the whole approach assumes background quoters use this same fixed-rel deterministic quoting ~14min cold start, to be a reliable backup)\n- Decided to gate trust in the rel estimate on its own stability: track variance/spread of recovered rel estimates over time \u2014 tight/stable readings                 "text": "Sorry, let me back up.\n\nWhen your quoter wants to place an order, it publishes a message onto NATS, something like \"add a bid at 592.\" \"Block for reply\" means: after publishing that message, your code stops and waits (holding execution, not moving to the next line) until the exchange sends something back confirming it, before continuing. Your thread is literally paused during that round trip: your message travels to the exchange, the exchange processes it, and its response travels back to you, then your code resumes.\n\nThe specific bug is that this pause currently happens *while holding `gMutex`*, the single lock that guards every instrument's state. So while your quoter is sitting there waiting on AAM6's order confirmation, nothing else can touch shared state at all, not AAU6's requote, not a driver fv update, nothing, because they all need that same lock and it's stuck being held by the paused AAM6 call. Whatever's queued behind it has to wait the full round-trip time before it can even start, which is exactly the kind of delay that turns \"we computed the right price\" into \"but it was already stale by the time we could act on it.\"\n\nThe alternative, \"fire-and-forget,\" means you publish the order and immediately move on without waiting for anything, you'd find out it was accepted later, the normal way, through the same A/C market data messages you're already subscribed to and processing anyway. If your protocol supports that (you don't need anything back before you know what to do next), you never have to hold a lock across a network round-trip in the first place, and this whole problem mostly disappears.\n\nDoes that clear up what I meant? is from the actual simulation/exchange source, not just inspiration)\n- [stated] Found and read the taker's action logic: every 0.05-0.5s it reads BBO from one randomly chosen instrument but submits its order to an independently, separately randomly chosen instrument (two separate random.choice(ALL) calls, not tied together) \u2014 meaning taker orders are frequently priced using a different instrument's book than the one they're actually submitted to, a likely source of noisy/mispriced fills distinct from the mover's behavior; taker order price is aggressive/marketable (ask+0-6 ticks or bid-0-6 ticks) and size is skewed toward small values (1 + int(20*random()**2), squared-uniform distribution concentrates near small sizes)\n- [stated] Ran own-book microprice change and compared against previous rolling-mean baseline: AAH6 results are similar (fair-value estimation was never the dominant AAH6 problem \u2014 confirms the mover's walk mechanism, not stale pricing, is the main AAH6 loss driver); AAM6 results got worse than the rolling-mean baseline (confirms the piggyback hypothesis \u2014 AAM6/AAU6's own book is thin/noisy and disconnected from the price the dominant background quoters actually use, so an accurate own-book estimate is a confident estimate of the wrong thing)\n- [stated] Decided on the AAM6/AAU6 fix: regress each piggyback instrument on the driving instrument (AAM6 = intercept + hedge_ratio*AAH6 + residual, same direction as the true generative relationship AAM6 = AAH6 + rel found in the quoter source) and price off that regression instead of own-book microprice; will compute this as an incremental/rolling OLS in C++ (running sums n, \u03a3x, \u03a3y, \u03a3xy, \u03a3x\u00b2 updated per sample, O(1) per update) rather than in a separate Python process, both because strategy/ must not be Python per the task spec and because the incremental OLS is computationally trivial (cheaper than the existing rolling-mean/z-score logic already in C++)\n- [stated] Decided to keep own-book microprice as a cold-start fallback for the regression-based estimate, mirroring the existing rolling-mean \u2192 EX_META ref_price fallback pattern already in the quoter\n- [stated] Measured how long it takes to get enough samples for a statistically significant Engle-Granger p-value: captured ~816s (~13.6 min) of live session data, resampled to a 500ms cadence, yielding 1632 samples \u2014 this was the point p-values first became reliably significant (consistent with the earlier finding that small/underpowered samples gave misleadingly insignificant results); concluded the 500ms-spaced sampling cadence (not raw tick data, which is highly autocorrelated and would inflate sample count without adding independent information) is what makes the p-value trustworthy, so decided to sample into the regression's rolling buffer at a fixed ~500ms cadence rather than feeding every raw BBO tick, and to treat ~13-14 minutes as the expected cold-start duration before trusting the regression, falling back to own-book microprice until then\n- [stated] Plan to generalize driver detection beyond the known AAH6 case: regress instruments against each other to find which instrument (Y) reliably explains multiple others (X1, X2...); flagged that contemporaneous-only regression can't distinguish a true driver from a fellow piggybacker (since two piggybackers of the same driver will also correlate with each other), so lead-lag structure (checking whether Y_{t-1} predicts X_t about as well as Y_t does) may be needed to confirm direction if generalizing beyond the AAH6-known-driver case\n- [stated] Root cause for AAH6 losses identified as being run over by the mover repeatedly: loss-triggered recalibration was making this worse, not better, because recalibrating after a bad fill resets fair value toward the price the mover just imposed, then requoting there puts the quoter right back in the mover's path \u2014 decided this needs a dedicated walk-detection/defense mechanism rather than adjusting the recalibration loss threshold\n- [stated] Decided on a mover walk-detector for AAH6 based on consecutive same-side adverse fills in a short window (e.g. 2+ fills on the same side within one requote cycle) as the primary signal, since it directly mirrors the confirmed mechanism (mover eats resting depth on one side via rapid marketable orders); response on trigger is to cancel/pull the resting order on that side and pause repricing on that side for a cooldown period, rather than immediately recalibrating and requoting into the same path; considered book-imbalance-via-microprice-divergence and rate-of-BBO-change as secondary/refinement signals if time allows\n- [stated] Decided on a clean separation of responsibilities: the quoter only defends (pulls/pauses quotes when it detects it's being run over), and actual position flattening stays entirely the hedger's job \u2014 the quoter will not self-flatten by crossing the spread\n- [stated] Current status: microprice (own-book) implemented and tested; regression-based piggyback pricing for AAM6/AAU6 and the AAH6 walk-detector are both designed but not yet implemented; hedger has a design (per-instrument independent flattening, patient/passive triggering informed by mean-reversion half-lives) but no code written yet",

                "text": "That code changes everything for the AAM6/AAU6 problem. This isn't a statistical relationship to estimate via regression at all \u2014 it's a **deterministic quoting rule**: the bot computes `center = round(fair_value(AAH6) + rel)` and requotes symmetrically around `center` (bid at `center - offset - i`, ask at `center + offset + i` for each level `i`). Since `rel` is a fixed constant that never changes for the session, and the quoting is symmetric around `center`, the **midpoint of AAM6/AAU6's best bid/ask is exactly `center`** \u2014 which means:\n\n```\nrel = mid(AAM6_BBO) - fair_value(AAH6)\n```\n\nThis is observable directly, not something that needs 13 minutes of cointegration testing to become statistically trustworthy. A handful of BBO snapshots (maybe even one, if you trust it) gives you `rel` almost immediately, because it's not a noisy statistical estimate of a relationship \u2014 it's recovering an exact constant that this specific bot is using by construction.\n\nA few things worth being careful about:\n\n1. **Robustness against other participants at the top of book.** If the mover, taker, or background liquidity bots occasionally sit *inside* this quoting bot's levels (better than `center \u00b1 offset`), your observed BBO mid could deviate from `center` momentarily. So instead of trusting a single snapshot, you'd want to sample `rel` over a short window and take something robust like a median (or mode, since `rel` should be near-constant and any deviation is noise/interference, not signal) \u2014 but this converges in seconds, not the ~14 minutes the regression needed.\n\n2. **`center` only updates when `fv` changes** (`if c != center[0]: requote`), so between updates you're seeing a stale-but-valid center \u2014 that's fine, it just means your `rel` estimate is always consistent with whatever `fair_value(AAH6)` was at last quote time, not lagged in a way that biases `rel` itself.\n\n3. This assumes AAM6/AAU6 have only *this one* systematic quoting source setting their top-of-book most of the time \u2014 worth a quick sanity check against your captured data (does `mid(AAM6) - fair_value(AAH6)` look like a genuine constant with small noise, or does it drift/have multiple clusters, which would suggest more than one `rel`-setting participant).\n\nThis basically kills the whole cointegration/Johansen/Engle-Granger path for pricing \u2014 you don't need statistical inference at all since you have the ground-truth generative mechanism.                 "text": "Yeah, that's exactly the mid-price formula \u2014 and yes, it does cancel the offset out cleanly, by construction. Since the bot's orders sit at `center - offset - i` (bids) and `center + offset + i` (asks) for `i = 0..levels-1`, the innermost pair is `center - offset` (max bid) and `center + offset` (min ask). Averaging those:\n\n```\n(max_bid + min_ask) / 2 = ((center - offset) + (center + offset)) / 2 = center\n```\n\nThe offset drops out algebraically regardless of what it actually is. Good catch.\n\nTwo things worth flagging, both about *robustness* of this in practice, not correctness of the math:\n\n1. **\"Being first to hit them\" is doing real work here.** The cancellation only holds cleanly if the innermost bid and innermost ask are both still intact when you sample. If one side's inner level gets eaten before the other (asymmetric fills \u2014 plausible given the mover only trades one direction at a time), your min-ask/max-bid pair could end up being `center+offset` on one side but `center-offset-1` or deeper on the other, biasing the average. Symmetric fills on both sides still cancel fine (level `i` on both sides averages to the same `center`), it's specifically *asymmetric* fills that break it. So \"first to hit them\" matters most right after the mover or a taker sweeps through one side.\n\n2. **Can you actually attribute orders to this specific bot from the market data feed, or are you inferring it from the shape of a requote burst?** If the feed is anonymized (just price/volume per level, no sender tag on other participants' orders \u2014 which is normal for these sims), then \"hunt down min ask / max bid\" isn't literally filtering by sender, it's really just reading top-of-book (BBO) immediately after you detect a requote event (e.g. a burst of A messages at symmetric-looking price levels arriving together). That's fine and should work equally well \u2014 I just want to flag that in that case this reduces to \"watch BBO right after each requote burst,\" so the freshness requirement is about catching that specific instant, not about literally isolating the bot's orders from others'. Worth confirming against PROTOCOL.md whether order messages carry any owner/sender info to outside subscribers, since that changes how you'd implement the detection (watch aggregate BBO right after a burst vs. actually filter by attributed sender).\n\n`rel = fv - c` \u2014 right, matches what we landed on last time, just now with a solid method for getting `c` cheaply per requote event instead of averaging over a window.\n\nQuoting a tick or two inside `rel \u00b1 offset` to sit ahead of them makes sense given you now know their center almost exactly \u2014 the main risk there is adverse selection if `fair_value(AAH6)` moves between the moment you compute `c`/`rel` and the moment your own quote actually posts, since you're now deliberately quoting *tight*, closer to true fair value, with less cushion than the background bot's own `offset` gives it. sized to eat exactly the resting depth between current price and target plus a 20% buffer \u2014 so \"sweeps\" are not a separate behavior from \"walking,\" just the large-magnitude tail of the same mechanism; decided this should be built into the quoter (detecting in-progress mover walks / reacting to them) rather than treated as a separate task\n- Found a fair_value() reference implementation (likely the exchange's own fair-value/reference-price definition) using a microprice formula: falls back to simple mid when spread >= 2 ticks or when both book-side volumes are zero, otherwise computes (bid*ask_vol + ask*bid_vol)/(bid_vol+ask_vol) \u2014 decided to switch the quoter's fair value calc to this microprice approach (confirmed this snippet is from the actual simulation/exchange source, not just inspiration)\n- Found and read the taker's action logic: every 0.05-0.5s it reads BBO from one randomly chosen instrument but submits its order to an independently, separately randomly chosen instrument (two separate random.choice(ALL) calls, not tied together) \u2014 meaning taker orders are frequently priced using a different instrument's book than the one they're actually submitted to, a likely source of noisy/mispriced fills distinct from the mover's behavior; taker order price is aggressive/marketable (ask+0-6 ticks or bid-0-6 ticks) and size is skewed toward small values (1 + int(20*random()**2), squared-uniform distribution concentrates near small sizes)\n- Ran own-book microprice change and compared against previous rolling-mean baseline: AAH6 results are similar (fair-value estimation was never the dominant AAH6 problem \u2014 confirms the mover's walk mechanism, not stale pricing, is the main AAH6 loss driver); AAM6 results got worse than the rolling-mean baseline (confirms the piggyback hypothesis \u2014 AAM6/AAU6's own book is thin/noisy and disconnected from the price the dominant background quoters actually use, so an accurate own-book estimate is a confident estimate of the wrong thing)\n- Decided on the AAM6/AAU6 fix: regress each piggyback instrument on the driving instrument (AAM6 = intercept + hedge_ratio*AAH6 + residual, same direction as the true generative relationship AAM6 = AAH6 + rel found in the quoter source) and price off that regression instead of own-book microprice; will compute this as an incremental/rolling OLS in C++ (running sums n, \u03a3x, \u03a3y, \u03a3xy, \u03a3x\u00b2 updated per sample, O(1) per update) rather than in a separate Python process, both because strategy/ must not be Python per the task spec and because the incremental OLS is computationally trivial (cheaper than the existing rolling-mean/z-score logic already in C++)\n- Decided to keep own-book microprice as a cold-start fallback for the regression-based estimate, mirroring the existing rolling-mean \u2192 EX_META ref_price fallback pattern already in the quoter\n- Measured how long it takes to get enough samples for a statistically significant Engle-Granger p-value: captured ~816s (~13.6 min) of live session data, resampled to a 500ms cadence, yielding 1632 samples \u2014 this was the point p-values first became reliably significant (consistent with the earlier finding that small/underpowered samples gave misleadingly insignificant results); concluded the 500ms-spaced sampling cadence (not raw tick data, which is highly autocorrelated and would inflate sample count without adding independent information) is what makes the p-value trustworthy, so decided to sample into the regression's rolling buffer at a fixed ~500ms cadence rather than feeding every raw BBO tick, and to treat ~13-14 minutes as the expected cold-start duration before trusting the regression, falling back to own-book microprice until then\n- Plan to generalize driver detection beyond the known AAH6 case: regress instruments against each other to find which instrument (Y) reliably explains multiple others (X1, X2...); flagged that contemporaneous-only regression can't distinguish a true driver from a fellow piggybacker (since two piggybackers of the same driver will also correlate with each other), so lead-lag structure (checking whether Y_{t-1} predicts X_t about as well as Y_t does) may be needed to confirm direction if generalizing beyond the AAH6-known-driver case\n- Root cause for AAH6 losses identified as being run over by the mover repeatedly: loss-triggered recalibration was making this worse, not better, because recalibrating after a bad fill resets fair value toward the price the mover just imposed, then requoting there puts the quoter right back in the mover's path \u2014 decided this needs a dedicated walk-detection/defense mechanism rather than adjusting the recalibration loss threshold\n- Decided on a mover walk-detector for AAH6 based on consecutive same-side adverse fills in a short window (e.g. 2+ fills on the same side within one requote cycle) as the primary signal, since it directly mirrors the confirmed mechanism (mover eats resting depth on one side via rapid marketable orders); response on trigger is to cancel/pull the resting order on that side and pause repricing on that side for a cooldown period, rather than immediately recalibrating and requoting into the same path; considered book-imbalance-via-microprice-divergence and rate-of-BBO-change as secondary/refinement signals if time allows\n- Decided on a clean separation of responsibilities: the quoter only defends (pulls/pauses quotes when it detects it's being run over), and actual position flattening stays entirely the hedger's job \u2014 the quoter will not self-flatten by crossing the spread\n- Found and read the actual background quoter bot source for AAM6/AAU6: it computes `center = round(fair_value(AAH6) + rel)` each time fair_value(AAH6) changes, then requotes symmetrically around center (bid at center-offset-i, ask at center+offset+i per level) \u2014 rel is a fixed constant chosen once per contract at bot startup and never changes during the session\n- Decided to abandon the regression/cointegration approach for AAM6/AAU6 pricing in favor of directly recovering rel, since it's an exact deterministic constant (not a statistical relationship): rel = mid(AAM6_BBO) - fair_value(AAH6), observable almost immediately (a short robust sample, e.g. median over a small window, rather than the ~14min cointegration cold-start) rather than needing sustained data collection; plan to verify this against already-captured BBO CSV data before implementing\n- Settled offset-detection method for identifying driver vs piggyback instruments and recovering AAM6/AAU6 fair value: piggyback instruments should reliably regress onto the true driver instrument (used to ID which instrument is the driver when the number/identity of instruments in play isn't known in advance); once driver is identified, recover the background quoter bot's center per requote by taking (max_bid + min_ask)/2 across its innermost order levels immediately after detecting a requote burst \u2014 this cancels the bot's offset out algebraically regardless of its value, since orders sit symmetrically at center\u00b1offset\u00b1i; then rel = fair_value(driver) - center, and the quoter quotes a tick or two inside rel\u00b1offset to sit tighter than the background bots\n- Known risks/caveats on the offset-detection method, explicitly accepted: (1) requires being first to sample right after a requote burst \u2014 asymmetric fills on one side (e.g. from the mover hitting one side only) before sampling will bias the center estimate, though symmetric fills still cancel correctly; (2) works fine even if the market data feed is anonymized/lacks sender attribution, since it only needs aggregate BBO read right after a detected requote-burst event, not per-order attribution \u2014 but requires PROTOCOL.md to confirm individual order messages (A/C/E/T) arrive in a way that lets a requote burst be detected as a discrete event, not just a fully pre-aggregated BBO snapshot; (3) the whole approach assumes background quoters use this same fixed-rel deterministic quoting logic in the actual grading market, which is unverified and could be wrong, with no fast statistical fallback available if it is wrong (statistical/cointegration-based estimation takes too long, ~14min cold start, to be a reliable backup)\n- Decided to gate trust in the rel estimate on its own stability: track variance/spread of recovered rel estimates over time \u2014 tight/stable readings mean the deterministic-quoting assumption holds and the quoter trusts rel and quotes tight; noisy/drifting readings signal the assumption is broken, triggering fallback to the existing own-book microprice/rolling-mean approach (accepting worse edge) rather than trusting a wrong deterministic assumption\n- Current status: microprice (own-book) implemented and tested; rel-based direct pricing for AAM6/AAU6 (settled design above, replacing the earlier regression plan) and the AAH6 walk-detector are both designed but not yet implemented; hedger has a design (per-instrument independent                         "extracted_content": "// skeleton.cpp\n//\n// Quoter (strategy/) seat:\n//   1. Connect to NATS at $NATS_URL\n//   2. Discover every instrument in EX_META\n//   3. Per instrument: track a rolling lookback window of mid-prices,\n//      compute realized volatility (rolling stddev) and a z-score of the\n//      current mid vs. the rolling mean\n//   4. Quote fair value = rolling mean, spread sized off realized vol,\n//      skewed by our own inventory and a *bounded* z-score tilt (never a\n//      directional trigger \u2014 see computeQuotes())\n//   5. Track PnL per instrument from our own fills; if PnL since the last\n//      recalibration breaches a loss threshold, recalibrate that\n//      instrument's parameters; otherwise leave them alone\n//   6. Requote on a timer (not per-tick), respecting a min interval as a\n//      crude max_tps throttle\n//\n// Still missing / TODO before this is production-safe:\n//   - Proper max_tps handling (currently a fixed 250ms cycle; should read\n//     EX_META's max_tps per instrument once its semantics for 0 are\n//     confirmed \u2014 see NOTES.md open question)\n//   - Order id uniqueness only holds within ~10k orders per instrument per\n//     process lifetime (4-char feed + 4-digit wrapping sequence)\n//   - No graceful shutdown / order cancellation on exit yet\n//   - Position/PnL uses a simple running-average cost method, not\n//     lot-level accounting \u2014 fine for risk purposes, not for precise P&L\n//\n// Build: see CMakeLists.txt / Dockerfile.\n\n#include <nats.h>\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <deque>\n#include <fstream>\n#include <iostream>\n#include <map>\n#include <mutex>\n#include <set>\n#include <sstream>\n#include <string>\n#include <thread>\n#include <vector>\n\n// Reads env var with a fallback default, since the grading harness injects\n// real values but local dev needs something sane.\nstatic const char* envOr(const char* name, const char* fallback) {\n    const char* v = std::getenv(name);\n    return (v && v[0] != '\\0') ? v : fallback;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Instrument metadata (parsed from EX_META)\n// ============================================================================\n\nstruct InstrumentMeta {\n    long long ticksize = 0;\n    long long ref_price = 0;\n    long long band = 0;\n    long long min_volume = 0;\n    long long max_volume = 0;\n    long long position_limit = 0;\n    long long max_tps = 0;\n    long long last_traded_price = 0;\n};\n\nstatic InstrumentMeta parseMeta(const std::string& value) {\n    InstrumentMeta meta;\n    std::stringstream ss(value);\n    std::string pair;\n    while (ss >> pair) {\n        auto eq = pair.find('=');\n        if (eq == std::string::npos) continue;\n        std::string key = pair.substr(0, eq);\n        long long val = std::atoll(pair.substr(eq + 1).c_str());\n        if (key == \"ticksize\") meta.ticksize = val;\n        else if (key == \"ref_price\") meta.ref_price = val;\n        else if (key == \"band\") meta.band = val;\n        else if (key == \"min_volume\") meta.min_volume = val;\n        else if (key == \"max_volume\") meta.max_volume = val;\n        else if (key == \"position_limit\") meta.position_limit = val;\n        else if (key == \"max_tps\") meta.max_tps = val;\n        else if (key == \"last_traded_price\") meta.last_traded_price = val;\n    }\n    return meta;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Per-instrument state\n// ============================================================================\n\nstruct InstrumentState {\n    std::string feed;\n    InstrumentMeta meta;\n\n    // Latest BBO snapshot. -1 means \"no quote on that side\".\n    long long bidPx = -1, bidVol = -1, askPx = -1, askVol = -1;\n\n    // --- Rolling lookback window for realized vol / z-score ---\n    // Sized in number of mid-price samples, not wall-clock time. Since BBO\n    // update frequency isn't constant, a fixed sample count gives a more\n    // stable window than a fixed time span would.\n    std::deque<double> priceWindow;\n    size_t lookback = 200;\n    double rollingStd = 0.0;\n    double zscore = 0.0;\n\n    // --- Adaptive strategy parameters ---\n    // Set at recalibration time only (startup + loss-triggered), not on\n    // every tick, to avoid chasing noise. spreadMultiplier scales realized\n    // vol into a half-spread;       // lifetime, informational\n    double pnlSinceRecalib = 0.0;   // reset at every recalibration\n    std::set<std::string> seenMatchIds; // avoid double-processing a fill\n\n    // --- Resting order bookkeeping (one bid, one ask per instrument) ---\n    std::string restingBidId, restingAskId;\n    long long restingBidPx = -1, restingAskPx = -1;\n    long long orderSeq = 0;\n\n    std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point lastRequote{};\n};\n\nstatic std::map<std::string, InstrumentState> instruments;\nstatic std::mutex instrumentsMutex;\n\nstatic std::ofstream logFile;\nstatic std::mutex logMutex;\n\n// Dedicated PnL/loss log, separate from the raw market-data dump above so\n// you can actually eyeball or plot PnL without filtering out BBO/MD noise.\nstatic std::ofstream pnlFile;\nstatic std::mutex pnlMutex;\n\nstatic natsConnection* gConn = nullptr;\nstatic std::string gSender;\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Small helpers\n// ============================================================================\n\nstatic std::vector<std::string> splitFields(const char* data, int len) {\n    std::string payload(data, len);\n    std::stringstream ss(payload);\n    std::vector<std::string> fields;\n    std::string word;\n    while (ss >> word) fields.push_back(word);\n    return fields;\n}\n\nstatic void writeRow(const char* sourceTag, const char* subject,\n                      const std::vector<std::string>& fields) {\n    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(logMutex);\n    logFile << sourceTag << \",\" << subject;\n    for (const auto& f : fields) logFile << \",\" << f;\n    logFile << \"\\n\";\n    logFile.flush();\n}\n\n// \"SENDER:ORDERID\" -> SENDER\nstatic std::string senderOf(const std::string& partyTag) {\n    auto colon = partyTag.find(':');\n    return (colon == std::string::npos) ? partyTag : partyTag.substr(0, colon);\n}\n\n// std::clamp requires C++17; using a local helper instead of bumping the\n// project's C++ standard, since that's unconfirmed elsewhere in the build.\ntemplate <typename T>\nstatic T clampValue(T v, T lo, T hi) {\n    return (v < lo) ? lo : (v > hi) ? hi : v;\n}\n\nstatic long long nowNanos() {\n    auto now = std::chrono::system_clock::now().time_since_epoch();\n    return std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(now).count();\n}\n\n// Microprice: volume-weighted mid that leans toward whichever side has\n// less resting volume (the thinner side is closer to trading through).\n// Weight each price by the volume on the OPPOSITE side \u2014 heavy bid volume\n// pulls the estimate toward the ask, not the bid, since a deep bid queue\n// means more has to trade before price can move down.\n// Returns -1 if either side of the book is currently empty; caller falls\n// back to ref_price in that case (see fairValue()).\nstatic double microprice(const InstrumentState& st) {\n    if (st.bidPx < 0 || st.askPx < 0) return -1.0;\n    if (st.bidVol <= 0 || st.askVol <= 0) {\n        return (static_cast<double>(st.bidPx) + static_cast<double>(st.askPx)) / 2.0;\n    }\n    double bidVol = static_cast<double>(st.bidVol);\n    double askVol = static_cast<double>(st.askVol);\n    return (static_cast<double>(st.bidPx) * askVol + static_cast<double>(st.askPx) * bidVol)\n           / (bidVol + askVol);\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Fair value\n// ============================================================================\n\n// Fair value source: rolling mean once the lookback window has enough\n// samples; EX_META's ref_price as a fallback before that. Without this,\n// the quoter would sit out entirely at startup even though EX_META hands\n// us a usable reference price immediately. Resolves the earlier open\n// design question (\"fair value source: BBO mid vs. ref_price/\n// last_traded_price with fallback\") as: rolling mean is primary, ref_price\n// is the cold-start fallback only, not a permanent blend.\n// Fair value source: microprice when both sides of the book are present;\n// EX_META's ref_price as the cold-start / one-sided-book fallback.\n// Replaces the old rolling-mean-of-mid estimate. The rolling window/mean\n// is still tracked below (updateRollingStats) \u2014 it now feeds only the\n// realized-vol spread sizing and the z-score mean-reversion tilt in\n// computeQuotes(), not the fair value itself.\nstatic double fairValue(const InstrumentState& st) {\n    double mp = microprice(st);\n    if (mp >= 0.0) return mp;\n    return static_cast<double>(st.meta.ref_price);\n}\n\n// Current mid from the latest BBO, if both sides are present; falls back to\n// fairValue() (rolling mean, or EX_META's ref_price during cold start) if\n// one side is currently empty, so PnL marks don't go stale/undefined just\n// because the book is one-sided for a tick.\nstatic double currentMid(const InstrumentState& st) {\n    if (st.bidPx >= 0 && st.askPx >= 0) {\n        return (static_cast<double>(st.bidPx) + static_cast<double>(st.askPx)) / 2.0;\n    }\n    return fairValue(st);\n}\n\n// Unrealized PnL: mark our open position at the current mid vs. our average\n// entry price. This is what makes a losing OPEN position visible \u2014 realizedPnL\n// alone stays at 0 until you actually reduce/close, so a position bleeding\n// against you looks invisible without this.\nstatic double unrealizedPnL(const InstrumentState& st) {\n    if (st.position == 0) return 0.0;\n    double mid = currentMid(st);\n    double pnlPerUnit = (st.position > 0) ? (mid - st.avgEntryPrice) : (st.avgEntryPrice - mid);\n    return pnlPerUnit * std::abs(static_cast<double>(st.position));\n}\n\n// Writes one row to the dedicated PnL/loss csv (data/pnl.csv), writing the\n// header once on first use. event_type is \"FILL\" (one row per fill) or\n// \"SNAPSHOT\" (one row per periodic tick, so you can see PnL drift even with\n// no fills, e.g. an open position bleeding against you).\n//\n// counterparty / counterpartyRole are only meaningful on FILL rows: \"-\" is\n// passed for both on SNAPSHOT rows since no trade happened that tick.\n// counterpartyRole is from OUR perspective on that fill:\n//   \"AGGRESSOR\" -> we hit their resting order (we initiated)\n//   \"PASSIVE\"   -> our resting order got hit (they filled us \u2014 this is\n//                  \"who's been fulfilling my orders\")\nstatic bool pnlHeaderWritten = false;\nstatic void writePnlRow(const char* eventType, const InstrumentState& st,\n                         double pnlDelta, const char* side, long long price,\n                         long long volume, const std::string& counterparty,\n                         const char* counterpartyRole) {\n    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(pnlMutex);\n    if (!pnlHeaderWritten) {\n        pnlFile << \"ts,event_type,feed,side,fill_price,fill_volume,counterparty,\"\n                    \"counterparty_role,position,avg_entry_price,mid,ref_price,\"\n                    \"realized_pnl,unrealized_pnl,total_pnl,pnl_since_recalib\\n\";\n        pnlHeaderWritten = true;\n    }\n    double unreal = unrealizedPnL(st);\n    pnlFile << nowNanos() << \",\" << eventType << \",\" << st.feed << \",\"\n             << side << \",\" << price << \",\" << volume << \",\"\n             << counterparty << \",\" << counterpartyRole << \",\"\n             << st.position << \",\" << st.avgEntryPrice << \",\" << currentMid(st) << \",\"\n             << st.meta.ref_price << \",\" << st.realizedPnL << \",\" << unreal << \",\"\n             << (st.realizedPnL + unreal) << \",\" << st.pnlSinceRecalib << \"\\n\";\n    pnlFile.flush();\n    (void)pnlDelta; // kept as a param for FILL rows if you want to log it separately later\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Rolling stats\n// ============================================================================\n\nstatic void updateRollingStats(InstrumentState& st) {\n    if (st.bidPx < 0 || st.askPx < 0) return; // need both sides for a mid\n    double mid = (static_cast<double>(st.bidPx) + static_cast<double>(st.askPx)) / 2.0;\n\n    st.priceWindow.push_back(mid);\n    if (st.priceWindow.size() > st.lookback) st.priceWindow.pop_front();\n    if (st.priceWindow.size() < 2) return;\n\n    // Local mean is just a variance intermediate now -- not stored, not\n    // used as a baseline for anything (z-score below uses microprice).\n    double sum = 0.0;\n    for (double p : st.priceWindow) sum += p;\n    double localMean = sum / static_cast<double>(st.priceWindow.size());\n\n    double sqSum = 0.0;\n    for (double p : st.priceWindow) sqSum += (p - localMean) * (p - localMean);\n    double variance = sqSum / static_cast<double>(st.priceWindow.size() - 1);\n    st.rollingStd = std::sqrt(variance);\n\n    // Z-score: deviation of the plain mid from the microprice (volume-\n    // weighted mid), normalized by realized vol. Measures how far the mid\n    // is sitting from where book imbalance says it \"should\" be, rather\n    // than deviation from a rolling average.\n    double mp = microprice(st);\n    st.zscore = (st.rollingStd > 1e-9 && mp >= 0.0) ? (mid - mp) / st.rollingStd : 0.0;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Recalibration (loss-triggered, not continuous)\n// ============================================================================\n\nstatic void recalibrate(InstrumentState& st) {\n    st.spreadMultiplier = 2.0;\n    st.skewPerUnitInventory = (st.meta.position_limit > 0)\n        ? (st.rollingStd / static_cast<double>(st.meta.position_limit))\n        : 0.0;\n    st.pnlSinceRecalib = 0.0;\n    printf(\"[%s] recalibrated: mean=%.2f std=%.4f spreadMult=%.2f skewPerUnit=%.6f\\n\",\n           st.feed.c_str(), st.rollingStd, st.spreadMultiplier,\n           st.skewPerUnitInventory);\n}\n\n// Loss threshold, in price units, since the last recalibration. Expressed\n// as a multiple of ticksize so it scales sensibly across instruments with\n// different price levels \u2014 20 ticks is a starting assumption, not a\n// validated number; tune against pilot PnL data.\nstatic double lossThreshold(const InstrumentState& st) {\n    return -20.0 * static_cast<double>(st.meta.ticksize);\n}\n\nstatic void checkAndRecalibrate(InstrumentState& st) {\n    if (st.pnlSinceRecalib < lossThreshold(st)) {\n        printf(\"[%s] loss threshold breached (pnlSinceRecalib=%.2f) \u2014 recalibrating\\n\",\n               st.feed.c_str(), st.pnlSinceRecalib);\n        recalibrate(st);\n    }\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Fill processing (own fills only)\n// ============================================================================\n\n// side: 'B' or 'S' \u2014 the side WE traded (not the aggressor's side from the\n// wire message; caller resolves that before calling this).\n// counterparty: sender ID of whoever was on the other side of this fill.\n// counterpartyRole: \"AGGRESSOR\" if WE hit THEM, \"PASSIVE\" if THEY hit US\n// (i.e. \"who's been fulfilling my orders\" \u2014 see writePnlRow's doc comment).\nstatic void applyFill(InstrumentState& st, char side, long long price, long long volume,\n                       const std::string& counterparty, const char* counterpartyRole) {\n    double signedVol = (side == 'B') ? static_cast<double>(volume) : -static_cast<double>(volume);\n    long long positionBefore = st.position;\n    long long newPosition = st.position + static_cast<long long>(signedVol);\n    double pnlDelta = 0.0;\n\n    if (st.position == 0 || (st.position > 0) == (signedVol > 0)) {\n        // Adding to (or opening) a position: extend average entry price.\n        double totalCost = st.avgEntryPrice * std::abs(static_cast<double>(st.position))\n                          + static_cast<double>(price) * std::abs(signedVol);\n        double totalVol = std::abs(static_cast<double>(st.position)) + std::abs(signedVol);\n        st.avgEntryPrice = (totalVol > 0) ? (totalCost / totalVol) : static_cast<double>(price);\n    } else {\n        // Reducing or flipping a position: realize PnL on the closed part.\n        double closedVol = std::min(std::abs(static_cast<double>(st.position)), std::abs(signedVol));\n        double pnlPerUnit = (st.position > 0)\n            ? (static_cast<double>(price) - st.avgEntryPrice)\n            : (st.avgEntryPrice - static_cast<double>(price));\n        pnlDelta = pnlPerUnit * closedVol;\n        st.realizedPnL += pnlDelta;\n        st.pnlSinceRecalib += pnlDelta;\n\n        if (std::abs(signedVol) > std::abs(static_cast<double>(st.position))) {\n            // Flipped through flat \u2014 new position takes on the fill price.\n            st.avgEntryPrice = static_cast<double>(price);\n        }\n    }\n\n    st.position = newPosition;\n\n    // FILL row: ts, feed, side, price, volume, positionBefore, positionAfter,\n    // pnlDelta (this fill only), realizedPnL (lifetime), pnlSinceRecalib.\n    // Left unchanged (no counterparty fields) so any existing parser of\n    // bbo_data.csv's FILL tag doesn't break on a field-count change --\n    // counterparty tracking is added to pnl.csv only (see writePnlRow call\n    // below), which is the dedicated, actively-evolving own-strategy log.\n    {\n        std::stringstream ss;\n        ss << nowNanos() << \",\" << st.feed << \",\" << side << \",\" << price << \",\"\n           << volume << \",\" << positionBefore << \",\" << newPosition << \",\"\n           << pnlDelta << \",\" << st.realizedPnL << \",\" << st.pnlSinceRecalib;\n        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(logMutex);\n        logFile << \"FILL,\" << ss.str() << \"\\n\";\n        logFile.flush();\n    }\n\n    // Dedicated PnL log row for this fill \u2014 carries who the counterparty\n    // was and whether they hit us or we hit them.\n    writePnlRow(\"FILL\", st, pnlDelta, std::string(1, side).c_str(), price, volume,\n                counterparty, counterpartyRole);\n\n    checkAndRecalibrate(st);\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Quote computation\n// ============================================================================\n\nstruct Quote {\n    bool valid = false;\n    long long bidPx = -1, askPx = -1, vol = -1;\n};\n\nstatic Quote computeQuotes(const InstrumentState& st) {\n    Quote q;\n    if (st.meta.ticksize <= 0) return q;\n    // No usable price at all \u2014 no rolling data AND no ref_price from\n    // EX_META (would be 0 if the key were missing/malformed). Stay out.\n    // No usable fair value at all: book is one-sided/empty (microprice\n    // undefined) AND EX_META gave no ref_price fallback either. Stay out.\n    if (microprice(st) < 0.0 && st.meta.ref_price <= 0) return q;       \n\n    double fv = fairValue(st);\n\n    // rollingStd is 0 until the window has >= 2 samples, so before that,\n    // half-spread is entirely the tick-based floor below \u2014 this is the\n    // cold-start case where we're quoting off ref_price, not realized vol.\n    double halfSpread = std::max(\n        st.spreadMultiplier * st.rollingStd / 2.0,\n        static_cast<double>(st.minSpreadTicks * st.meta.ticksize) / 2.0);\n\n    // Inventory skew: lean the fair value away from our current position so\n    // resting quotes naturally bias toward flattening.\n    double inventorySkew = -st.skewPerUnitInventory * static_cast<double>(st.position);\n\n    // Z-score tilt: bounded to a quarter of the half-spread and clamped to\n    // +/-2 std, so it nudges quoting rather than becoming a directional\n    // signal. This is a mean-reversion bias on a market-making quote, not\n    // a \"take a position because z-score says so\" trigger.\n    double clampedZ = clampValue(st.zscore, -2.0, 2.0);\n    double zscoreTilt = -clampedZ * (halfSpread * 0.25);\n\n    double adjustedFV = fv + inventorySkew + zscoreTilt;\n\n    long long bidPx = static_cast<long long>(std::round((adjustedFV - halfSpread) / st.meta.ticksize))\n                       * st.meta.ticksize;\n    long long askPx = static_cast<long long>(std::round((adjustedFV + halfSpread) / st.meta.ticksize))\n                       * st.meta.ticksize;\n\n    long long lo = st.meta.ref_price - st.meta.band;\n    long long hi = st.meta.ref_price + st.meta.band;\n    bidPx = clampValue(bidPx, lo, hi);\n    askPx = clampValue(askPx, lo, hi);\n    if (askPx <= bidPx) askPx = bidPx + st.meta.ticksize;\n\n    // Base size: placeholder fixed size within instrument limits. Sizing\n    // strategy (e.g. scaling down as position approaches position_limit)\n    // is a further refinement, not yet implemented.\n    long long baseSize = 10;\n    long long vol = std::max(st.meta.min_volume, std::min(st.meta.max_volume, baseSize));\n\n    q.valid = true;\n    q.bidPx = bidPx;\n    q.askPx = askPx;\n    q.vol = vol;\n    return q;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Order entry (ex.req.<SENDER> request/reply)\n// ============================================================================\n\nstatic std::string nextOrderId(InstrumentState& st) {\n    // 4-char feed (feeds are always 4 chars per PROTOCOL.md) + 4-digit\n    // wrapping sequence = 8 chars, unique per feed for ~10k live orders.\n    char buf[9];\n    long long seq = (st.orderSeq++) % 10000;\n    snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), \"%.4s%04lld\", st.feed.c_str(), seq);\n    return std::string(buf);\n}\n\n// Sends \"<SENDER> A <FEED> <id> <B|S> <volume> <price> <L>\" and returns\n// true if the exchange accepted it (reply starts with \"Y\").\nstatic bool addOrder(const std::string& feed, const std::string& orderId,\n                      char side, long long volume, long long price) {\n    char msg[256];\n    snprintf(msg, sizeof(msg), \"%s A %s %s %c %lld %lld L\",\n              gSender.c_str(), feed.c_str(), orderId.c_str(), side, volume, price);\n\n    char subject[64];\n    snprintf(subject, sizeof(subject), \"ex.req.%s\", gSender.c_str());\n\n    natsMsg* reply = nullptr;\n    natsStatus s = natsConnection_RequestString(&reply, gConn, subject, msg, 2000);\n    if (s != NATS_OK) {\n        printf(\"[%s] natsMsg_Destroy(reply);\n\n    if (!replyStr.empty() && replyStr[0] == 'Y') return true;\n    printf(\"[%s] addOrder rejected: %s\\n\", feed.c_str(), replyStr.c_str());\n    return false;\n}\n\n// Sends \"<SENDER> C <FEED> <id>\".\nstatic bool cancelOrder(const std::string& feed, const std::string& orderId) {\n    if (orderId.empty()) return true;\n    char msg[256];\n    snprintf(msg, for a mid\n    double mid = (static_cast<double>(st.bidPx) + static_cast<double>(st.askPx)) / 2.0;\n\n    st.priceWindow.push_back(mid);\n    if (st.priceWindow.size() > st.lookback) for (double p : st.priceWindow) sqSum += (p - localMean) * (p - localMean);\n    double variance = sqSum / static_cast<double>(st.priceWindow.size() - 1);\n    st.rollingStd = std::sqrt(variance);\n\n           st.avgEntryPrice = static_cast<double>(price);\n        }\n    }\n\n    st.position = newPosition;\n\n    // --- Mover walk-detector bookkeeping ---\n    // Record this fill's side/time,     }\n    }\n\n    // FILL row: ts, feed, side, price, volume, positionBefore, positionAfter,\n    // pnlDelta (this fill only), realizedPnL (lifetime), pnlSinceRecalib.\n    // Left unchanged (no ============================================================================\n\nstruct Quote {\n    bool valid = false;\n    long long bidPx = -1, askPx = -1, vol = -1;\n};\n\nstatic Quote computeQuotes(const InstrumentState& st) {\n    Quote q;\n    if (st.meta.ticksize <= 0) return q;\n\n    bool piggybackTrusted = (!gDriverFeed.empty() && st.feed != gDriverFeed && st.relTrusted);\n\n    // No usable fair value at all: book is one-sided/empty (microprice\n    // undefined) AND EX_META gave no ref_price fallback either AND we\n    // don't have a trusted rel-based price to fall back Stay out.\n    if (microprice(st) < 0.0 && st.meta.ref_price <= 0 && !piggybackTrusted) return q;\n\n    double fv = fairValue(st);\n\n    // rollingStd is 0 until the window has >= 2 samples, so before that,\n    // half-spread is entirely the tick-based floor below \u2014 this is the\n    // cold-start case where we're quoting off ref_price, not realized vol.\n    double halfSpread;\n    if (piggybackTrusted) {\n        // Priority: quote a couple ticks inside the background bot's own\n        // recovered half-spread (observedOffset), so we sit ahead of them\n        // on a price we're confident is exactly what they're using too --\n        // rather than the vol-based spread, which doesn't make sense to\n        // apply here since this fair value isn't derived from our own\n        // (thin/noisy) book at all. Floored at the usual minSpreadTicks so\n        // we never quote unreasonably tight or cross.\n        double insideBy = 2.0 * static_cast<double>(st.meta.ticksize);\n        halfSpread = std::max(st.observedOffset - insideBy,\n                               static_cast<double>(st.minSpreadTicks) * st.meta.ticksize / 2.0);\n    } else {\n        halfSpread = std::max(\n            st.spreadMultiplier * st.rollingStd / 2.0,\n            static_cast<double>(st.minSpreadTicks * st.meta.ticksize) / 2.0);\n    }\n\n    // Inventory skew: lean the fair value away from our current position so\n    // resting quotes naturally bias toward flattening.\n    double inventorySkew = -st.skewPerUnitInventory * static_cast<double>(st.position);\n\n    // Z-score tilt: bounded to a quarter of the half-spread and clamped to\n    // +/-2 std, so it nudges quoting rather than becoming a directional\n    // signal. This is a mean-reversion bias on a market-making quote, not\n    // a \"take a position because z-score says so\" trigger. Skipped for a\n    // trusted piggyback price -- the z-score is computed off this\n    // instrument's own (thin/disconnected) book, which isn't a meaningful\n    // signal once we're pricing off the driver instead.\n    double zscoreTilt = 0.0;\n    if (!piggybackTrusted) {\n        double clampedZ = clampValue(st.zscore, -2.0, 2.0);\n        zscoreTilt = -clampedZ * (halfSpread * 0.25);\n    }\n\n    double adjustedFV = fv + inventorySkew + zscoreTilt;\n\n    long long bidPx = static_cast<long long>(std::round((adjustedFV - halfSpread) / st.meta.ticksize))\n                       * st.meta.ticksize;\n    long long askPx = static_cast<long long>(std::round((adjustedFV + halfSpread) / st.meta.ticksize))\n                       * st.meta.ticksize;\n\n    long long lo = st.meta.ref_price - st.meta.band;\n    long long hi = st.meta.ref_price + st.meta.band;\n    bidPx = clampValue(bidPx, lo, hi);\n    askPx = clampValue(askPx, lo, hi);\n    if (askPx <= bidPx) askPx = bidPx + st.meta.ticksize;\n\n    // Base size: placeholder fixed size within instrument limits. Sizing\n    // strategy (e.g. scaling down as position approaches position_limit)\n    // is a further refinement, not yet implemented.\n    long long baseSize = 10;\n    long long vol = std::max(st.meta.min_volume, std::min(st.meta.max_volume, baseSize));\n\n    q.valid = true;\n    q.bidPx = bidPx;\n    q.askPx = askPx;\n    q.vol = vol;\n    return q;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Order entry (ex.req.<SENDER> request/reply)\n// ============================================================================\n\nstatic std::string nextOrderId(InstrumentState& st) {\n    // 4-char feed (feeds are always 4 chars per PROTOCOL.md) + 4-digit\n    // wrapping sequence = 8 chars, unique per feed for ~10k live orders.\n    char buf[9];\n    long long seq = (st.orderSeq++) % 10000;\n    snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), \"%.4s%04lld\", st.feed.c_str(), seq);\n    return std::string(buf);\n}\n\n// Sends \"<SENDER> A <FEED> <id> <B|S> <volume> <price> <L>\" and returns\n// true if the exchange accepted it (reply starts with natsMsg_Destroy(reply);\n\n    if (!replyStr.empty() && replyStr[0] == 'Y') return true;\n    printf(\"[%s] addOrder rejected: %s\\n\", feed.c_str(), replyStr.c_str());\n    return false;\n}\n\n// Sends \"<SENDER> C <FEED> <id>\".\nstatic bool cancelOrder(const std::string& feed, const std::string& orderId) {\n    if (orderId.empty()) return true;\n    char msg[256];\n    snprintf(msg, replyStr[0] == 'Y';\n}\n\n// Cancel-and-replace both sides if the desired quote differs meaningfully\n// from what's currently resting. Called on a timer, not per-tick. Also\n// enforces the mover walk-detector's per-side pause: a paused side is\n// pulled (if resting) and left flat until its cooldown expires, regardless\n// of what computeQuotes() would otherwise want to post there.\nstatic void requoteInstrument(InstrumentState& st) {\n    Quote q = computeQuotes(st);\n    if (!q.valid) return;\n\n    auto nowTp = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();\n    bool bidPaused = nowTp < st.bidPausedUntil;\n    bool askPaused = nowTp < st.askPausedUntil;\n\n    // Pull any resting order sitting on a now-paused side -- the whole\n    // point of the walk-detector is ============================================================================\\n// Instrument metadata (parsed from EX_META)\\n// ============================================================================\\n\\nstruct InstrumentMeta {\\n    long long ticksize = 0;\\n    long long ref_price = 0;\\n    long long band = 0;\\n    long long min_volume = 0;\\n    long long max_volume = 0;\\n    long long position_limit = 0;\\n    long long max_tps = 0;\\n    long long last_traded_price = 0;\\n};\\n\\nstatic InstrumentMeta ============================================================================\\n// Per-instrument state\\n// ============================================================================\\n\\nstruct InstrumentState {\\n    std::string feed;\\n    InstrumentMeta meta;\\n\\n    // Latest BBO snapshot. -1 means \\\"no quote on that side\\\".\\n    long long bidPx = -1, bidVol = -1, askPx = -1, On trigger we pull\\n    // that side and pause requoting it for a cooldown, instead of\\n    // recalibrating back into the same path (recalibrating after a bad\\n    // fill drags fair value toward the price the mover just imposed --\\n    // requoting there puts us right back in its way).\\n    std::deque<std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point> bidFillTimes, askFillTimes;\\n    std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point bidPausedUntil{}, askPausedUntil{};\\n\\n    // --- Rel-based piggyback pricing (for non-driver instruments) ---\\n    // Recovered whenever this instrument's BBO shows a fresh two-sided\\n    // requote (both bid and ask move together -- the signature of the\\n    // background quoter bot cancelling and replacing around a new\\n    // center). center = (bid+ask)/2 cancels the bot's own offset out\\n    // algebraically regardless of its value, since its orders sit\\n    // symmetrically at center +/- offset +/- i. rel is then\\n    // driver_fair_value - center; This matches the\\n// confirmed mechanism directly -- the mover only trades the front\\n// instrument, so real trade volume concentrates there; piggyback\\n// instruments only see the comparatively thin flow of background\\n// liquidity/takers trading against the quoter bots' derived price.\\n// Protected by instrumentsMutex (always updated/read under that lock).\\nstatic std::map<std::string, long long> tradeCounts;\\nstatic std::string gDriverFeed;\\nstatic constexpr long long kDriverWarmupTrades = 30;\\nstatic constexpr double kDriverMargin = 1.3; // leader must beat current driver by this factor to take over -- avoids flip-flopping on a noisy early lead\\n\\n// Mover walk-detector tuning. kWalkWindow ~= one requote cycle, since\\n// that's the timescale on which the mover's rapid marketable orders eat\\n// through one side. kWalkCooldown is deliberately longer than a single\\n// requote cycle so we don't immediately re-post into an active walk.\\nstatic constexpr int kWalkFillThreshold = 2;\\nstatic constexpr std::chrono::milliseconds kWalkWindow{250};\\nstatic constexpr std::chrono::milliseconds kWalkCooldown{2000};\\n\\n// Re-evaluate which instrument is the driver. Sticky by design\\n// (kDriverMargin, kDriverWarmupTrades) so early noise or a temporary lead\\n// doesn't cause rel trackers on piggyback instruments to reset or\\n// flip-flop between candidate drivers.\\nstatic void updateDriver() {\\n    long long total = 0;\\n    std::string best;\\n    long long bestCount = -1;\\n    for (auto& [feed, count] : tradeCounts) {\\n        total += count;\\n        if (count > bestCount) { bestCount = count; best = feed; }\\n    }\\n    if (total < kDriverWarmupTrades || best.empty()) return;\\n\\n    if (gDriverFeed.empty()) {\\n        gDriverFeed = best;\\n        printf(\\\"[driver] initial pick: %s (%lld trades observed so far)\\\\n\\\", best.c_str(), bestCount);\\n        return;\\n    }\\n    long long currentCount = tradeCounts.count(gDriverFeed) ? tradeCounts[gDriverFeed] : 0;\\n    if (best != gDriverFeed &&\\n        static_cast<double>(bestCount) > kDriverMargin * static_cast<double>(std::max<long long>(currentCount, 1))) {\\n        printf(\\\"[driver] switching %s -> %s (%lld vs %lld trades)\\\\n\\\",\\n               gDriverFeed.c_str(), best.c_str(), bestCount, currentCount);\\n        gDriverFeed = best;\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n// ============================================================================\\n// Small helpers\\n// ============================================================================\\n\\nstatic std::vector<std::string> splitFields(const char* data, int len) {\\n    std::string payload(data, len);\\n    std::stringstream ss(payload);\\n    std::vector<std::string> fields;\\n    std::string word;\\n    while (ss >> word) fields.push_back(word);\\n    return fields;\\n}\\n\\nstatic void writeRow(const char* sourceTag, const char* subject,\\n                      const std::vector<std::string>& fields) {\\n    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(logMutex);\\n    logFile << sourceTag << \\\",\\\" << subject;\\n    for (const auto& f : fields) logFile << \\\",\\\" << f;\\n    logFile << \\\"\\\\n\\\";\\n    logFile.flush();\\n}\\n\\n// \\\"SENDER:ORDERID\\\" -> SENDER\\nstatic std::string senderOf(const std::string& partyTag) {\\n    auto colon = partyTag.find(':');\\n    return (colon == std::string::npos) ? partyTag : partyTag.substr(0, colon);\\n}\\n\\n// std::clamp requires C++17; using a local helper instead of bumping the\\n// project's C++ standard, since that's unconfirmed elsewhere in the build.\\ntemplate <typename T>\\nstatic T clampValue(T v, T lo, T hi) {\\n    return (v < lo) ? lo : (v > hi) ? hi : v;\\n}\\n\\nstatic long long nowNanos() {\\n    auto now = std::chrono::system_clock::now().time_since_epoch();\\n    return std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(now).count();\\n}\\n\\n// Microprice: volume-weighted mid that leans toward whichever side has\\n// less resting volume (the thinner side is closer to trading through).\\n// Weight each price by the volume on the OPPOSITE side \\u2014 heavy bid volume\\n// pulls the estimate toward the ask, not the bid, since a deep bid queue\\n// means more has to trade before price can move down.\\n// Returns -1 if either side of the book is currently empty; caller falls\\n// back to ref_price in that case (see fairValue()).\\nstatic double microprice(const InstrumentState& st) {\\n    if (st.bidPx < 0 || st.askPx < 0) return -1.0;\\n    if (st.bidVol <= 0 || st.askVol <= 0) {\\n        return (static_cast<double>(st.bidPx) + static_cast<double>(st.askPx)) / 2.0;\\n    }\\n    double bidVol = static_cast<double>(st.bidVol);\\n    double askVol = static_cast<double>(st.askVol);\\n    return (static_cast<double>(st.bidPx) * askVol + static_cast<double>(st.askPx) * bidVol)\\n           / (bidVol + askVol);\\n}\\n\\n// ============================================================================\\n// Fair value\\n// ============================================================================\\n\\n// Fair value source, in priority order:\\n//   1. This is a\\n//      deterministic price (recovered from the background bots' own\\n//      fixed-offset quoting rule), not a statistical estimate, so it\\n//      takes priority over the instrument's own order book whenever\\n//      available -- see the settled offset-detection design.\\n//   2. (mid - st.avgEntryPrice) : (st.avgEntryPrice - mid);\\n    return pnlPerUnit * std::abs(static_cast<double>(st.position));\\n}\\n\\n// Writes one row to the dedicated PnL/loss csv (data/pnl.csv), writing the\\n// header once on first use. event_type is \\\"FILL\\\" (one row per fill) or\\n// \\\"SNAPSHOT\\\" (one row per periodic tick, so you can see PnL drift even with\\n// no fills, e.g. an filled us \\u2014 this is\\n//                  \\\"who's been fulfilling my orders\\\")\\nstatic bool pnlHeaderWritten = false;\\nstatic void writePnlRow(const char* eventType, const InstrumentState& counterpartyRole) {\\n    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(pnlMutex);\\n    if (!pnlHeaderWritten) {\\n        pnlFile << \\\"ts,event_type,feed,side,fill_price,fill_volume,counterparty,\\\"\\n                    \\\"counterparty_role,position,avg_entry_price,mid,ref_price,\\\"\\n                    \\\"realized_pnl,unrealized_pnl,total_pnl,pnl_since_recalib\\\\n\\\";\\n        pnlHeaderWritten = \\\",\\\" << volume << \\\",\\\"\\n             << counterparty << \\\",\\\" << counterpartyRole << \\\",\\\"\\n             << st.position << \\\",\\\" << st.avgEntryPrice << \\\",\\\" <<
