                "uuid": "01a05c5f-f799-789f-8a2d-ae4404d1de1a",
                "text": "Good catch on the fv(driver) point \u2014 noted, not relevant anymore since you're reading c directly off their book now.\n\nThe core issue with your old design wasn't that concurrency is inherently unavoidable in this problem \u2014 it's that you *introduced* concurrency you didn't need. Multiple threads (callback paths, a 100ms safety-net timer, a worker queue) all touching the same struct meant you needed mutexes to keep them from corrupting each other. Race conditions aren't a law of nature here \u2014 they're a consequence of having more than one thread mutate shared state. Remove the second thread, and the race condition doesn't need guarding against, because it no longer exists.\n\n**So: go single-threaded, event-driven, no timers.** One thread processes NATS messages strictly in arrival order, one at a time, fully, before touching the next. No background thread. No wall-clock polling loop. This alone eliminates the need for mutexes entirely \u2014 there's nothing left to race.\n\nHere's the state machine that gets you burst-completion detection inside that model:\n\n**Per instrument, keyed by the LP's known sender ID** (you already do sender-based filtering, so this is cheap):\n\n```\nstruct LpBurstState {\n    bool    active;\n    Price   best_bid, best_ask;   // running best seen this burst\n    bool    seen_bid, seen_ask;\n    Time    last_msg_time;        // timestamp of last A/X from this LP on this instrument\n};\n```\n\n**On every incoming message** (still just one message at a time, on the one thread):\n\n1. If it's a Cancel/CancelAll from the LP sender on this instrument \u2192 reset that instrument's `LpBurstState` (clear seen flags, mark `active = true`, stamp `last_msg_time`). This is \"burst started.\"\n2. If it's an Add from the LP sender on this instrument \u2192 update `best_bid`/`best_ask` accordingly, set the corresponding `seen_bid`/`seen_ask` flag, stamp `last_msg_time`.\n3. **Before doing anything else with *any* message** (this is the trick that replaces a timer thread): check whether any instrument currently has `active == true` and `now - last_msg_time > debounce_window`. If so, and both `seen_bid` and `seen_ask` are true, the burst is done \u2014 compute `mid = (best_bid + best_ask) / 2`, mark `active = false`, and that's your fresh c. This check costs nothing (it's just a comparison over however many instruments you're tracking) and it piggybacks on messages you're already processing, so there's no separate polling loop needed.\n\nBecause everything above happens inline in the single message-processing path, there is no moment where two code paths can observe or mutate `LpBurstState` at the same time. No mutex needed \u2014 not because you've cleverly avoided a race, but because there's structurally only ever one reader/writer.\n\n**On the symmetry check you asked about \u2014 you probably don't need it.** You were originally thinking about symmetry because it was useful for confirming the *whole ladder* (needed for rel recovery, and for computing your own quote width off their reach). But now you only need best bid and best ask to get mid. As soon as you've seen one Add on each side after a cancel, and the burst has gone quiet, you have what you need \u2014 you don't have to wait for the full ladder to land, and you don't have to verify shape. If you want extra confidence that you're not catching a still-completing burst, the debounce window is doing that job already; a symmetry check would be redundant complexity for what you're actually using this signal for.\n\nOne edge case worth handling explicitly: if the LP only posts one side before you decide to act (e.g. a partial fill event on their side triggers a re-quote of just one side, if that's possible in this protocol), your `seen_bid`/`seen_ask` gate correctly makes you wait rather than computing mid off a stale/missing side. If you go fully single-threaded, event-driven, processing one NATS message at a time before touching the next, there is no concurrency problem left to solve. Not \"handled by careful locking\" \u2014 structurally absent. No mutexes needed anywhere.\n\n**Market race conditions (an economics problem)** \u2014 the world changing between when you observe something and when your order lands. This is real, unavoidable, and not fixable with better code architecture. It's just risk you price in or design around. Your taker-order worry and your \"hope it isn't immediately filled\" worry are both this category, not concurrency.\n\nGoing through your points:\n\n**Debounce window** \u2014 yes, inferred empirically, not hardcoded. You already have captured burst data from earlier sessions: look at inter-arrival time between consecutive Add messages *within* a burst vs. the gap *before the next burst starts*. Set debounce comfortably above typical intra-burst spacing, comfortably below typical inter-burst spacing. Since your design is now single-threaded, this is just an offline stats question, not something you need runtime coordination to compute. You can also refine it online per-LP as you observe more bursts, but that's a value update, not a new thread.\n\n**Taker orders confounding your read of \"the mid\"** \u2014 real risk, but the fix is about *which messages you trust*, not concurrency. If you compute your `LpBurstState.best_bid/best_ask` strictly from Add messages sent by the *LP's own sender ID* (which you're already filtering by), a taker order resting briefly during the LP's cancel/repost gap simply never touches your state \u2014 it's not the LP, so it doesn't update your tracked best_bid/best_ask. Your c calculation stays clean regardless of what taker noise is happening in the aggregate book.\n\nWhere the taker actually matters is at the moment you go to *cross* \u2014 the real book (not your filtered LP-only view) might have a taker order sitting at or ahead of the LP's fresh price, absorbing part of what you were aiming for. That's not a bug to fix, it's fill risk to accept: check the live top-of-book at submission time for sizing, but don't let it corrupt your fair-value read.\n\n**fv(driver) changing while your quotes are resting** \u2014 your instinct (immediate rescind) is right and it's simple in a single-threaded model: that market-data message triggers cancel as literally the next action, synchronously, before the message loop moves to anything else. No race, because nothing else can act between \"detect drift\" and \"cancel\" \u2014 you're the only thread.\n\n**\"Shit can get messy\" / cross-contamination while LPs reprice** \u2014 you've already solved this without realizing it: since you gate your own action on *that specific LP's burst-completion signal*, and you treat each piggyback/LP independently, you never act on stale state. requotes are full cancel-all/add-all reposting the same ladder shape, fire only when rounded c crosses to a new integer value. Ladder symmetric: bid=c-offset-i, ask=c+offset+i for i in [0,levels); offset/levels/volume fixed per contract at startup (volume ~ randint(2,6))\n- fair_value() reference formula: falls back to mid when spread >= 2 ticks or both book-side volumes are zero, else microprice (bid*ask_vol + ask*bid_vol)/(bid_vol+ask_vol)\n- Taker bot: reads BBO from one randomly chosen instrument, submits to an independently chosen instrument (mismatched book pricing), aggressive/marketable pricing, size skewed small (1 + int(20*random()**2))\n- EDA: all three instruments show significant individual mean-reversion (half-lives ~16-36s, needs ~13-14 min cold start for significance); cross-instrument cointegration abandoned as unnecessary \u2014 hedger does independent per-instrument flattening, not cross-instrument netting\n\n## Strategy evolution (settled design)\n- Decided the quoter will trade every discovered instrument, and the hedger will flatten each instrument's position independently (not net exposure across correlated instruments)\n- Settled quoter approach: treat driver (AAH6) as unquoted signal-only; discover driver/piggyback clusters at runtime (lagged correlation + stability debounce); recover each piggyback's rel from the LP's own requote-burst ladder; quote symmetrically around c = fv(driver)+rel, fixed +/-N ticks outside the LP's max ladder reach; own order volume = LP's observed per-level volume minus 1\n- Settled hedger approach: separate Python process, subscribes to all instruments' fill streams to reconstruct desk-wide position, converts piggyback positions to driver-equivalent via published rel/offset (DESK_STATE KV), nets into one combined exposure; small dead-band near zero; urgency scales continuously with |net exposure|/position_limit; reacts per-fill not on timer. Fix identified (not yet applied): route safety-net loop through requestRequote() too, making worker thread the sole caller\n\n## Quoting-too-tight losses \u2192 pivot to wide/defensive quoting (settled)\n- Diagnosed root cause: quoting inside/near LP's ladder meant getting crossed immediately on LP reprice, refilling at a worse price \u2014 guaranteed loss each cycle\n- Confirmed via PnL CSV: a single mid-price gap of ~161 units in a ~1.3ms window explained a run of 11+ consecutive losing fills \u2014 a genuine large gap event, not routine ladder-overlap\n- Settled fix: quote one tick beyond LP's farthest ladder reach (c \u00b1 (offset+levels-1) \u00b1 1); size = LP's observed per-level volume minus 1; cancel/recalc/re-check-trigger/post-one-at-a-time/re-check-between-each-add sequence, abort-and-restart if c moves mid-post; reprice trigger = observe c itself (LP's rounding-boundary rule) independently per-piggyback\n- Jump/gap circuit breaker settled to live in the quoter (not hedger, since hedger can't cancel a still-resting stale order): per-instrument paused flag set when a jump is detected, checked at existing checkDriverFvUpdate call sites\n- Detection metric settled: track live gap |resting_px - c| continuously (not delta-between-consecutive-c-polls, since a shock's move can arrive across several smaller updates)\n\n## Rel recovery ABANDONED \u2014 pivot to new design (current, supersedes rel-recovery thread below)\n- Decided rel recovery is fundamentally unreliable (concurrency/latency-dependent, inconsistent convergence) and is being dropped entirely; reasoning: rel-based edge required winning a speed/timing race against LPs which isn't achievable, so pivoting from \"win on speed\" to \"win on price accuracy and smart quoting\"\n- New pricing approach: no longer need rel or fv(driver)+rel at all \u2014 LP's ladder is symmetric (best bid = c-offset, best ask = c+offset), so mid(best bid, best ask) read directly off the LP's own freshly-posted book equals c exactly\n- New trigger logic: round(fv(driver)) changing from previous iteration is a proxy \"reprice imminent\" flag (not exact, since it ignores rel's effect on the rounding boundary, but fires at roughly the right rate) \u2014 on trigger, immediately cancel own resting quotes on affected piggybacks and wait for the LP's fresh post\n- New fill approach: actively cross the LP's freshly-posted ladder immediately after it completes, rather than resting passively \u2014 edge source is the LP's own post being stale-by-construction (driver kept moving during the LP's multi-message repost latency), not a speed race\n- Burst-completion detection settled: per-instrument state (best_bid/best_ask/seen_bid/seen_ask/last_msg_time), reset on LP cancel, updated on LP Add messages (filtered by LP's own sender ID only, not aggregate BBO, to avoid taker-order contamination), considered complete when quiet for a debounce window and both sides seen; debounce window to be inferred empirically from captured historical burst inter-arrival-time data\n- Decided to go fully single-threaded/event-driven (one thread processes NATS messages strictly in arrival order) specifically to eliminate the concurrency/mutex infrastructure that caused problems in the old design \u2014 no worker thread, no timer thread, no mutexes needed since there is structurally only one reader/writer of state\n- Distinguishes market race conditions (state changing between observation and action \u2014 inherent risk, not fixable by architecture) from software concurrency races (fixed by going single-threaded) \u2014 taker orders potentially resting during an LP's cancel/repost gap and fill-priority risk when crossing are treated as the former, not bugs to engineer around\n- Open item: sequencing between own-quote cancel-ack and firing the new crossing order \u2014 considering a per-instrument \"awaiting own cancel ack\" flag to avoid double-side exposure, not yet decided/implemented\n- Plan to keep learning each LP's offset/levels from observed history as a secondary confidence/sanity check on burst completion, not as a requirement (no longer needed to compute c)\n- Noted as a pinned-for-later risk: entire clustering/driver-signal design assumes a many-piggyback-to-one-driver relationship holds; if instruments turn out unrelated at grading time there's no fallback plan yet\n\n## [SUPERSEDED] Old rel-recovery debugging thread (abandoned, kept for history)\n- Symptom before abandoning: rel samples scattered wildly (121.5, 105.0, 15.5, -77.5 across consecutive samples) with sdTicks increasing (46\u219251+) as more samples accumulated \u2014 signature of a bias/mixture problem, not insufficient sample count\n- Key insight that contributed to the decision to abandon: NATS gives no cross-subscriber delivery-order/timing guarantee, so LP's fv(driver)-at-decision-time and live-read fv(driver) aren't guaranteed to agree even off the same subscription \u2014 recovering rel precisely was fighting causality itself\n\n## Process notes\n- User expressed a moment of doubt about strategic thinking ability after several rounds on the rel-recovery sub-problem\n- Pipeline now has 8+ sequential stages (discovery, debounce, burst detection, contamination guard, causal anchor, rel trust gate, concurrency-safe queue, jump detection) \u2014 worth reassessing against actual grading bar (profitable + low risk) once current debugging thread resolves\n</content>\n",

                            "file_text": "# Quoter Design Spec \u2014 Cannon Capital TRV Task\n\n## 1. Summary\n\nThe quoter no longer attempts to recover each piggyback's `rel` constant against the driver instrument. Instead, it treats a change in `round(fv(driver))` as a coarse \"reprice imminent\" signal, pulls its own resting quotes, waits for the LP to finish reposting its ladder, reads the LP's fresh best bid/ask directly off the book, and actively crosses that fresh quote. The edge comes from the LP's own post being stale by construction (the driver keeps moving during the LP's multi-message repost), not from outrunning anyone on raw speed.\n\nThe whole system runs single-threaded and event-driven: one thread processes NATS messages strictly in arrival order, one at a time, to completion, before touching the next message. This removes the need for mutexes or worker/timer threads entirely \u2014 there is structurally only ever one reader/writer of state.\n\n## 2. What changed and why\n\n| Old approach | New approach | Reason |\n|---|---|---|\n| Recover `rel` per piggyback from LP's requote burst; quote at `c = fv(driver) + rel` | Read `c` directly as `mid(best_bid, best_ask)` off the LP's own fresh ladder | `rel` recovery was fighting NATS's lack of cross-subscriber ordering guarantees \u2014 inconsistent, unreliable, effectively an unwinnable timing problem |\n| Quote wide/defensively, outside the LP's ladder reach, and wait to get filled passively | Actively cross the LP's ladder right after it finishes posting | Passive/defensive quoting turned into a speed race against LPs and takers that can't be won reliably; active crossing exploits the LP's inherent repost latency instead |\n| Multi-threaded: worker thread, 100ms safety-net timer thread, mutex-guarded shared struct | Single-threaded, event-driven message loop | Removes the source of concurrency bugs rather than patching around them \u2014 no shared-state races to guard against if there's only one thread |\n\n## 3. Core mechanism: reading `c` without `rel`\n\nThe LP's ladder is symmetric: `best_bid = c - offset`, `best_ask = c + offset`. Therefore:\n\n```\nmid(best_bid, best_ask) = c\n```\n\nNo `rel`, no driver fair-value formula, no timestamp reconstruction required \u2014 `c` is read directly off the LP's own posted prices once the repost is complete.\n\n## 4. Reprice trigger (approximate, and that's fine)\n\n- On every driver market-data message, recompute `round(fv(driver))`.\n- If it differs from the previous iteration's value, treat this as \"reprice imminent\" for every piggyback clustered to this driver.\n- This is a **proxy**, not the LP's exact trigger (`round(fv(driver) + rel)` crossing an integer) \u2014 it will fire slightly early or late relative to the true event. This is acceptable: the trigger's only job is \"get defensive now,\" not \"compute a precise price.\" Precision comes later, from directly observing the LP's fresh post.\n\n**On trigger, per affected piggyback:**\n1. Cancel all own resting orders on that instrument.\n2. Wait for own cancel-ack(s) before doing anything else on that instrument (see \u00a76 \u2014 avoids self-fills).\n3. Reset that instrument's burst-tracking state (\u00a75) and mark it \"awaiting LP burst.\"\n\n## 5. Burst-completion detection\n\nPer instrument, track LP-only state (filtered strictly by the LP's known sender ID \u2014 never the aggregate BBO feed, to avoid taker-order contamination):\n\n```\nstruct LpBurstState {\n    bool  active;\n    Price best_bid, best_ask;\n    bool  seen_bid, seen_ask;\n    Time  last_msg_time;\n};\n```\n\n- **On LP Cancel/CancelAll** (this instrument): reset `seen_bid`/`seen_ask` to false, set `active = true`, stamp `last_msg_time`.\n- **On LP Add** (this instrument): update `best_bid`/`best_ask` from that message, set the corresponding `seen_bid`/`seen_ask` flag, stamp `last_msg_time`.\n- **Completion check** (run cheaply on every incoming message, not on a timer): if `active` and `now - last_msg_time > debounce_window` and both `seen_bid` and `seen_ask` are true \u2192 burst is complete. Compute `c = mid(best_bid, best_ask)`, set `active = false`.\n\n**Debounce window:** inferred empirically from captured historical burst data \u2014 measure inter-arrival time between consecutive Add messages *within* a burst vs. the gap *before* the next burst starts. Set the window comfortably above typical intra-burst spacing and comfortably below typical inter-burst spacing. Can be refined online per-LP as more bursts are observed.\n\n**Why filter by LP sender ID only:** a taker order can transiently rest during the LP's cancel\u2192repost gap (its \"marketable\" price may not actually cross anything if the book is briefly empty). Filtering strictly to the LP's own Add messages means this never contaminates the computed `c`.\n\n## 6. Own-order sequencing (avoid self-fills)\n\nCancel-then-post must be strictly ordered per instrument to avoid crossing your own resting orders (has happened before):\n\n1. Reprice trigger fires \u2192 cancel own resting orders on this instrument.\n2. Enter `awaiting_own_cancel_ack` state for this instrument \u2014 no new orders submitted while in this state.\n3. Once cancel-ack(s) received \u2192 clear `awaiting_own_cancel_ack`, transition to `awaiting_lp_burst`.\n4. LP burst completes (\u00a75) \u2192 compute `c`, determine crossing price/side, submit new order.\n\nThis state is separate from `LpBurstState.active` \u2014 both must be clear before submitting a new order.\n\n## 7. Crossing logic\n\nOnce `c` is known (fresh, post-burst):\n- Determine crossing side and price from the LP's actual posted best bid/ask (not derived arithmetic \u2014 read the real numbers).\n- Check the live top-of-book at submission time, not just the LP-filtered view, since a taker order may be sitting at or ahead of the LP's price and will affect fill size/priority. This is fill risk to accept, not something to engineer around.\n- Submit sized to the LP's known per-level volume for that price level where knowable, otherwise a conservative default.\n\n## 8. Concurrency model\n\n- Single thread, strict in-order message processing.\n- No mutexes, no worker thread, no polling/timer thread.\n- Burst-completion check piggybacks on the normal message loop (cheap comparison run per incoming message) rather than a separate timer thread.\n- Distinguish explicitly between:\n  - **Software concurrency races** \u2014 eliminated by the single-threaded design.\n  - **Market races** (taker beating you to a fill, book state changing between observation and action) \u2014 real, unavoidable, accepted as risk rather than \"fixed.\"\n\n## 9. Secondary use of learned LP parameters\n\nOffset/levels per LP, learned from historical observation, are kept as an optional **confidence/sanity check** on burst completion (e.g. \"did we see the expected number of levels post\") \u2014 not a requirement. `c` no longer depends on them.\n\n## 10. Open items (not yet resolved)\n\n- **Fallback plan if the many-piggyback-to-one-driver clustering assumption doesn't hold** at grading time \u2014 no design yet; pinned for later.\n- Exact sizing rule when crossing (beyond \"LP's per-level volume as a starting point\").\n- Interaction with the hedger's DESK_STATE coordination signal \u2014 not revisited since the rel-recovery pivot; may need updating since `c` is now sourced differently.\n"

reasoning: rel-based edge required winning a speed/timing race against LPs which isn't achievable, so pivoting from \"win on speed\" to \"win on price accuracy and smart quoting\"\n- New pricing approach: no longer need rel or fv(driver)+rel at all \u2014 LP's ladder is symmetric (best bid = c-offset, best ask = c+offset), so mid(best bid, best ask) read directly off the LP's own freshly-posted book equals c exactly\n- New trigger logic: round(fv(driver)) changing from previous iteration is a proxy \"reprice imminent\" flag (not exact, since it ignores rel's effect on the rounding boundary, but fires at roughly the right rate) \u2014 on trigger, immediately cancel own resting quotes on affected piggybacks and wait for the LP's fresh post\n- New fill approach: actively cross the LP's freshly-posted ladder immediately after it completes, rather than resting passively \u2014 edge source is the LP's own post being stale-by-construction (driver kept moving during the LP's multi-message repost latency), not a speed race\n- Burst-completion detection settled: per-instrument state (best_bid/best_ask/seen_bid/seen_ask/last_msg_time), reset on LP cancel, updated on LP Add messages (filtered by LP's own sender ID only, not aggregate BBO, to avoid taker-order contamination), considered complete when quiet for a debounce window and both sides seen; debounce window to be inferred empirically from captured historical burst inter-arrival-time data\n- Decided to go fully single-threaded/event-driven (one thread processes NATS messages strictly in arrival order) specifically to eliminate the concurrency/mutex infrastructure that caused problems in the old design \u2014 no worker thread, no timer thread, no mutexes needed since there is structurally only one reader/writer of state\n- Distinguishes market race conditions (state changing between observation and action \u2014 inherent risk, not fixable by architecture) from software concurrency races (fixed by going single-threaded) \u2014 taker orders potentially resting during an LP's cancel/repost gap and fill-priority risk when crossing are treated as the former, not bugs to engineer around\n- Open item: sequencing between own-quote cancel-ack and firing the new crossing order \u2014 considering a per-instrument \"awaiting own cancel ack\" flag to avoid double-side exposure, not yet decided/implemented\n- Plan to keep learning each LP's offset/levels from observed history as a secondary confidence/sanity check on burst completion, not as a requirement (no longer needed to compute c)\n- Fallback plan sketch (partial, deferred for later): if piggybacks turn out unrelated to any driver, will still identify and exclude front-months from quoting entirely (considers trading them directly \"suicide\"); Not yet built \u2014 deliberately deferred so quoter-only runs isolate whether unmanaged position growth is the sole remaining problem\n- Clean separation settled: quoter only defends (pulls/pauses own quotes when threatened), never self-flattens by crossing the spread; all flattening is the hedger's job\n- Open unresolved hedger questions: concrete numeric position cap; whether hedger ever trades driver directly via IOC vs only through piggybacks; exact hedger-to-quoter coordination signal (proposed: hedger publishes urgency/action state to DESK_STATE); whether taker needs to react to hedger state\n\n## Quoter rewrite (quoter.cpp) \u2014 concurrency fixes made\n- Rewrote quoter per consolidated build spec: debounced cluster/driver locking, burst-triggered rel recovery, contamination guard with mover-camping escape hatch, continuous per-event driver fv tracking, fixed +/-N tick quoting clamped to meta.band, full print checklist for diagnosability\n- Found/fixed causal-mismatch bug: burst-processing used live fv(driver) instead of the fv the LP actually saw when it decided to reprice (no cross-subject ordering guarantee between driver/piggyback feeds); fixed via valueAtOrBefore() timestamp lookup anchored to burstTs\n- Found/fixed three concurrency hazards: (1) concurrent requoteInstrument() calls racing \u2014 fixed via queued requote requests (gPendingRequotes dedup set + single worker thread); (2) publishPairing/kvStore_PutString blocking call held gMutex \u2014 fixed by copying locals out, unlocking, doing blocking call unlocked, relocking; (3) runDiscoveryPass holds gMutex for full O(instruments\u00b2\u00d7lag) sweep every 2s \u2014 deferred as low-priority (one-time cold-start phase)\n- Code review found queue fix only partially closes the race: safety-net loop in main() (100ms tick) still calls requoteInstrument directly with its own lock, bypassing the queue. Fix identified (not yet applied): route safety-net loop through requestRequote() too, making worker thread the sole caller\n\n## Quoting-too-tight losses \u2192 pivot to wide/defensive quoting (settled)\n- Diagnosed root cause: quoting inside/near LP's ladder meant getting crossed immediately on LP reprice, refilling at a worse price \u2014 guaranteed loss each cycle\n- Confirmed via PnL CSV: a single mid-price gap of ~161 units in a ~1.3ms window explained a run of 11+ consecutive losing fills \u2014 a genuine large gap event, not routine ladder-overlap\n- Settled fix: quote one tick beyond LP's farthest ladder reach (c \u00b1 (offset+levels-1) \u00b1 1); size = LP's observed per-level volume minus 1; cancel/recalc/re-check-trigger/post-one-at-a-time/re-check-between-each-add sequence, abort-and-restart if c moves mid-post; reprice trigger = observe c itself (LP's rounding-boundary rule) independently per-piggyback\n- Jump/gap circuit breaker settled to live in the quoter (not hedger, since hedger can't cancel a still-resting stale order): per-instrument paused flag set when a jump is detected, checked at existing checkDriverFvUpdate call sites\n- Detection metric settled: track live gap |resting_px - c| continuously (not delta-between-consecutive-c-polls, since a shock's move can arrive across several smaller updates)\n\n## Rel recovery ABANDONED \u2014 pivot to new design (current, supersedes rel-recovery thread below)\n- Decided rel recovery is fundamentally unreliable (concurrency/latency-dependent, inconsistent convergence) and is being dropped entirely; reasoning: rel-based edge required winning a speed/timing race against LPs which isn't achievable, so pivoting from \"win on speed\" to \"win on price accuracy and smart quoting\"\n- New pricing approach: no longer need rel or fv(driver)+rel at all \u2014 LP's ladder is symmetric (best bid = c-offset, best ask = c+offset), so mid(best bid, best ask) read directly off the LP's own freshly-posted book equals c exactly\n- New trigger logic: round(fv(driver)) changing from previous iteration is a proxy \"reprice imminent\" flag (not exact, since it ignores rel's effect on the rounding boundary, but fires at roughly the right rate) \u2014 on trigger, immediately cancel own resting quotes on affected piggybacks and wait for the LP's fresh post\n- New fill approach: actively cross the LP's freshly-posted ladder immediately after it completes, rather than resting passively \u2014 edge source is the LP's own post being stale-by-construction (driver kept moving during the LP's multi-message repost latency), not a speed race\n- Burst-completion detection settled: per-instrument state (best_bid/best_ask/seen_bid/seen_ask/last_msg_time), reset on LP cancel, updated on LP Add messages (filtered by LP's own sender ID only, not aggregate BBO, to avoid taker-order contamination), considered complete when quiet for a debounce window and both sides seen; debounce window to be inferred empirically from captured historical burst inter-arrival-time data\n- Decided to go fully single-threaded/event-driven (one thread processes NATS messages strictly in arrival order) specifically to eliminate the concurrency/mutex infrastructure that caused problems in the old design \u2014 no worker thread, no timer thread, no mutexes needed since there is structurally only one reader/writer of state\n- Distinguishes market race conditions (state changing between observation and action \u2014 inherent risk, not fixable by architecture) from software concurrency races (fixed by going single-threaded) \u2014 taker orders potentially resting during an LP's cancel/repost gap and fill-priority risk when crossing are treated as the former, not bugs to engineer around\n- Open item: sequencing between own-quote cancel-ack and firing the new crossing order \u2014 considering a per-instrument \"awaiting own cancel ack\" flag to avoid double-side exposure, not yet decided/implemented\n- Decided crossing order volume will match the LP's own volume at that price level (not a fraction/minus-one adjustment like the old defensive-quoting design used)\n- Fallback plan sketch (partial, deferred for later): if piggybacks turn out unrelated to any driver, will still identify and exclude front-months from quoting entirely (considers trading them directly \"suicide\"); for unrelated back-months, considering entering the book only via mean-reversion when reversion looks imminent, rather than continuous two-sided quoting \u2014 not fully worked out, explicitly deprioritized until after the current design is built\n\n## [SUPERSEDED] Old rel-recovery debugging thread (abandoned, kept for history)\n- Symptom before abandoning: rel samples scattered wildly (121.5, 105.0, 15.5, -77.5 across consecutive samples) with sdTicks increasing (46\u219251+) as more samples accumulated \u2014 signature of a bias/mixture problem, not insufficient sample count\n- Key insight that contributed to the decision to abandon: NATS gives no cross-subscriber delivery-order/timing guarantee, so LP's fv(driver)-at-decision-time and live-read fv(driver) aren't guaranteed to agree even off the same subscription \u2014 recovering rel precisely was fighting causality itself\n\n## Process notes\n- User expressed a moment of doubt about strategic thinking ability after several rounds on the rel-recovery sub-problem\n- Pipeline now has 8+ sequential stages (discovery, debounce, burst detection, contamination guard, causal anchor, rel trust gate, concurrency-safe queue, jump detection) \u2014 worth reassessing against actual grading bar (profitable + low risk) once current debugging thread resolves\n</content>\n",

Ladder symmetric: bid=c-offset-i, ask=c+offset+i for i in [0,levels); offset/levels/volume fixed per contract at startup (volume ~ randint(2,6))\n- fair_value() reference formula: falls back to mid when spread >= 2 ticks or both book-side volumes are zero, else microprice (bid*ask_vol + ask*bid_vol)/(bid_vol+ask_vol)\n- Taker bot: reads BBO from one randomly chosen instrument, submits to an independently chosen instrument (mismatched book pricing), aggressive/marketable pricing, size skewed small (1 + int(20*random()**2))\n- EDA: all three instruments show significant individual mean-reversion (half-lives ~16-36s, needs ~13-14 min cold start for significance); cross-instrument cointegration abandoned as unnecessary \u2014 hedger does independent per-instrument flattening, not cross-instrument netting\n\n## Strategy evolution (settled design)\n- Decided the quoter will trade every discovered instrument, and the hedger will flatten each instrument's position independently (not net exposure across correlated instruments)\n- Settled quoter approach: treat driver (AAH6) as unquoted signal-only; discover driver/piggyback clusters at runtime (lagged correlation + stability debounce); recover each piggyback's rel from the LP's own requote-burst ladder; quote symmetrically around c = fv(driver)+rel, fixed +/-N ticks outside the LP's max ladder reach; own order volume = LP's observed per-level volume minus 1\n- Settled hedger approach: separate Python process, subscribes to all instruments' fill streams to reconstruct desk-wide position, converts piggyback positions to driver-equivalent via published rel/offset (DESK_STATE KV), nets into one combined exposure; small dead-band near zero; urgency scales continuously with |net exposure|/position_limit; reacts per-fill not on timer. Not yet built \u2014 deliberately deferred so quoter-only runs isolate whether unmanaged position growth is the sole remaining problem\n- Clean separation settled: quoter only defends (pulls/pauses own quotes when threatened), never self-flattens by crossing the spread; all flattening is the hedger's job\n- Open unresolved hedger questions: concrete numeric position cap; whether hedger ever trades driver directly via IOC vs only through piggybacks; exact hedger-to-quoter coordination signal (proposed: hedger publishes urgency/action state to DESK_STATE); whether taker needs to react to hedger state\n\n## Quoter rewrite (quoter.cpp) \u2014 concurrency fixes made\n- Rewrote quoter per consolidated build spec: debounced cluster/driver locking, burst-triggered rel recovery, contamination guard with mover-camping escape hatch, continuous per-event driver fv tracking, fixed +/-N tick quoting clamped to meta.band, full print checklist for diagnosability\n- Found/fixed causal-mismatch bug: burst-processing used live fv(driver) instead of the fv the LP actually saw when it decided to reprice (no cross-subject ordering guarantee between driver/piggyback feeds); fixed via valueAtOrBefore() timestamp lookup anchored to burstTs\n- Found/fixed three concurrency hazards: (1) concurrent requoteInstrument() calls racing \u2014 fixed via queued requote requests (gPendingRequotes dedup set + single worker thread); (2) publishPairing/kvStore_PutString blocking call held gMutex \u2014 fixed by copying locals out, unlocking, doing blocking call unlocked, relocking; (3) runDiscoveryPass holds gMutex for full O(instruments\u00b2\u00d7lag) sweep every 2s \u2014 deferred as low-priority (one-time cold-start phase)\n- Code review found queue fix only partially closes the race: safety-net loop in main() (100ms tick) still calls requoteInstrument directly with its own lock, bypassing the queue. Fix identified (not yet applied): route safety-net loop through requestRequote() too, making worker thread the sole caller\n\n## Quoting-too-tight losses \u2192 pivot to wide/defensive quoting (settled)\n- Diagnosed root cause: quoting inside/near LP's ladder meant getting crossed immediately on LP reprice, refilling at a worse price \u2014 guaranteed loss each cycle\n- Confirmed via PnL CSV: a single mid-price gap of ~161 units in a ~1.3ms window explained a run of 11+ consecutive losing fills \u2014 a genuine large gap event, not routine ladder-overlap\n- Settled fix: quote one tick beyond LP's farthest ladder reach (c \u00b1 (offset+levels-1) \u00b1 1); size = LP's observed per-level volume minus 1; cancel/recalc/re-check-trigger/post-one-at-a-time/re-check-between-each-add sequence, abort-and-restart if c moves mid-post; reprice trigger = observe c itself (LP's rounding-boundary rule) independently per-piggyback\n- Jump/gap circuit breaker settled to live in the quoter (not hedger, since hedger can't cancel a still-resting stale order): per-instrument paused flag set when a jump is detected, checked at existing checkDriverFvUpdate call sites\n- Detection metric settled: track live gap |resting_px - c| continuously (not delta-between-consecutive-c-polls, since a shock's move can arrive across several smaller updates)\n\n## Rel recovery ABANDONED \u2014 pivot to new design (current, supersedes rel-recovery thread below)\n- Decided rel recovery is fundamentally unreliable (concurrency/latency-dependent, inconsistent convergence) and is being dropped entirely; reasoning: rel-based edge required winning a speed/timing race against LPs which isn't achievable, so pivoting from \"win on speed\" to \"win on price accuracy and smart quoting\"\n- New pricing approach: no longer need rel or fv(driver)+rel at all \u2014 LP's ladder is symmetric (best bid = c-offset, best ask = c+offset), so mid(best bid, best ask) read directly off the LP's own freshly-posted book equals c exactly\n- New trigger logic: round(fv(driver)) changing from previous iteration is a proxy \"reprice imminent\" flag (not exact, since it ignores rel's effect on the rounding boundary, but fires at roughly the right rate) \u2014 on trigger, immediately cancel own resting quotes on affected piggybacks and wait for the LP's fresh post\n- New fill approach: actively cross the LP's freshly-posted ladder immediately after it completes, rather than resting passively \u2014 edge source is the LP's own post being stale-by-construction (driver kept moving during the LP's multi-message repost latency), not a speed race\n- Burst-completion detection settled: per-instrument state (best_bid/best_ask/seen_bid/seen_ask/last_msg_time), reset on LP cancel, updated on LP Add messages (filtered by LP's own sender ID only, not aggregate BBO, to avoid taker-order contamination), considered complete when quiet for a debounce window and both sides seen; debounce window to be inferred empirically from captured historical burst inter-arrival-time data\n- Decided to go fully single-threaded/event-driven (one thread processes NATS messages strictly in arrival order) specifically to eliminate the concurrency/mutex infrastructure that caused problems in the old design \u2014 no worker thread, no timer thread, no mutexes needed since there is structurally only one reader/writer of state\n- Distinguishes market race conditions (state changing between observation and action \u2014 inherent risk, not fixable by architecture) from software concurrency races (fixed by going single-threaded) \u2014 taker orders potentially resting during an LP's cancel/repost gap and fill-priority risk when crossing are treated as the former, not bugs to engineer around\n- Open item: sequencing between own-quote cancel-ack and firing the new crossing order \u2014 considering a per-instrument \"awaiting own cancel ack\" flag to avoid double-side exposure, not yet decided/implemented\n- Decided crossing order volume will match the LP's own volume at that price level (not a fraction/minus-one adjustment like the old defensive-quoting design used)\n- Fallback plan sketch (partial, deferred for later): if piggybacks turn out unrelated to any driver, will still identify and exclude front-months from quoting entirely (considers trading them directly \"suicide\"); for unrelated back-months, considering entering the book only via mean-reversion when reversion looks imminent, rather than continuous two-sided quoting \u2014 not fully worked out, explicitly deprioritized until after the current design is built\n\n## [SUPERSEDED] Old rel-recovery debugging thread (abandoned, kept for history)\n- Symptom before abandoning: rel samples scattered wildly (121.5, 105.0, 15.5, -77.5 across consecutive samples) with sdTicks increasing (46\u219251+) as more samples accumulated \u2014 signature of a bias/mixture problem, not insufficient sample count\n- Key insight that contributed to the decision to abandon: NATS gives no cross-subscriber delivery-order/timing guarantee, so LP's fv(driver)-at-decision-time and live-read fv(driver) aren't guaranteed to agree even off the same subscription \u2014 recovering rel precisely was fighting causality itself\n\n## Process notes\n- User expressed a moment of doubt about strategic thinking ability after several rounds on the rel-recovery sub-problem\n- Pipeline now has 8+ sequential stages (discovery, debounce, burst detection, contamination guard, causal anchor, rel trust gate, concurrency-safe queue, jump detection) \u2014 worth reassessing against actual grading bar (profitable + low risk) once current debugging thread resolves\n</content>\n",

                "text": "Good question to nail down explicitly, since it's the entire premise of the \"cross the LP\" strategy.\n\n**Basic mechanic:** when you cross (submit a marketable order that takes liquidity instead of resting), you don't profit from the trade itself in isolation \u2014 a single fill against a fair price is roughly zero-EV. You profit when the price you're crossing *at* is stale relative to where the instrument's true value has already moved. You're not betting on the trade going your way after the fact; you're catching a price that's already wrong the moment you take it.\n\n**In your specific setup:** the LP computes `c = round(fv(driver) + rel)` at the instant it decides to reprice, then takes some nonzero time to actually cancel its old ladder and post the new one (multiple sequential Add messages, protocol-limited to one at a time). During that repost window, the driver (AAH6) keeps moving. By the time the LP's fresh ladder lands, its center `c` reflects `fv(driver)` *as of a moment slightly in the past* \u2014 not the driver's current value.\n\nSo if you cross their fresh ask right after it posts, and the driver has since ticked up, you're buying at a price that's already below where the piggyback \"should\" be trading given the driver's current level. You're not guessing direction \u2014 you're exploiting a known, structural information lag: their quote is a snapshot of a slightly-stale fair value, and you're acting with a slightly-fresher one.\n\n**Where the profit actually shows up:** either (a) the piggyback's own price catches up to reflect the driver's new level shortly after (mark-to-market gain), or (b) you immediately have an edge to unwind the position against \u2014 since you know approximately where \"true\" fair value now sits, you're not stuck holding a directionless position, you know which way it's biased.\n\n**The condition that has to hold for this to work at all:** the driver's move during the LP's repost window has to be large enough, often enough, to beat your transaction/fill risk (partial fills, taker beating you to it, slippage). If the driver barely moves during that latency window, there's no edge to capture \u2014 you're just taking a random side of a fair trade. Worth sanity-checking against your captured data: how much does the driver typically move in the time between an LP's cancel and its last Add landing? That number is basically your expected edge per crossing trade, before costs.",

You're not guessing direction \u2014 you're exploiting a known, structural information lag: their quote is a snapshot of a slightly-stale fair value, and you're acting with a slightly-fresher one.\n\n**Where the profit actually shows up:** either (a) the piggyback's own price catches up to reflect the driver's new level shortly after (mark-to-market gain), or (b) you immediately have an edge to unwind the position against \u2014 since you know approximately where \"true\" fair value now sits, you're not stuck holding a directionless position, you know which way it's biased.\n\n**The condition that has to hold for this to work at all:** the driver's move during the LP's repost window has to be large enough, often enough, to beat your transaction/fill risk (partial fills, taker beating you to it, slippage). If the driver barely moves during that latency window, there's no edge to capture \u2014 you're just taking a random side of a fair trade. Worth sanity-checking against your captured data: how much does the driver typically move in the time between an LP's cancel and its last Add landing? That number is basically your expected edge per crossing trade, before costs.",

                        "file_type": "text/markdown",
                        "extracted_content": "# Quoter Design Spec \u2014 Cannon Capital TRV Task\n\n## 1. Summary\n\nThe quoter no longer attempts to recover each piggyback's `rel` constant against the driver instrument. Instead, it treats a change in `round(fv(driver))` as a coarse \"reprice imminent\" signal, pulls its own resting quotes, waits for the LP to finish reposting its ladder, reads the LP's fresh best bid/ask directly off the book, and actively crosses that fresh quote. The edge comes from the LP's own post being stale by construction (the driver keeps moving during the LP's multi-message repost), not from outrunning anyone on raw speed.\n\nThe whole system runs single-threaded and event-driven: one thread processes NATS messages strictly in arrival order, one at a time, to completion, before touching the next message. This removes the need for mutexes or worker/timer threads entirely \u2014 there is structurally only ever one reader/writer of state.\n\n## 2. What changed and why\n\n| Old approach | New approach | Reason |\n|---|---|---|\n| Recover `rel` per piggyback from LP's requote burst; quote at `c = fv(driver) + rel` | Read `c` directly as `mid(best_bid, best_ask)` off the LP's own fresh ladder | `rel` recovery was fighting NATS's lack of cross-subscriber ordering guarantees \u2014 inconsistent, unreliable, effectively an unwinnable timing problem |\n| Quote wide/defensively, outside the LP's ladder reach, and wait to get filled passively | Actively cross the LP's ladder right after it finishes posting | Passive/defensive quoting turned into a speed race against LPs and takers that can't be won reliably; active crossing exploits the LP's inherent repost latency instead |\n| Multi-threaded: worker thread, 100ms safety-net timer thread, mutex-guarded shared struct | Single-threaded, event-driven message loop | Removes the source of concurrency bugs rather than patching around them \u2014 no shared-state races to guard against if there's only one thread |\n\n## 3. Core mechanism: reading `c` without `rel`\n\nThe LP's ladder is symmetric: `best_bid = c - offset`, `best_ask = c + offset`. Therefore:\n\n```\nmid(best_bid, best_ask) = c\n```\n\nNo `rel`, no driver fair-value formula, no timestamp reconstruction required \u2014 `c` is read directly off the LP's own posted prices once the repost is complete.\n\n## 4. Reprice trigger (approximate, and that's fine)\n\n- On every driver market-data message, recompute `round(fv(driver))`.\n- If it differs from the previous iteration's value, treat this as \"reprice imminent\" for every piggyback clustered to this driver.\n- This is a **proxy**, not the LP's exact trigger (`round(fv(driver) + rel)` crossing an integer) \u2014 it will fire slightly early or late relative to the true event. This is acceptable: the trigger's only job is \"get defensive now,\" not \"compute a precise price.\" Precision comes later, from directly observing the LP's fresh post.\n\n**On trigger, per affected piggyback:**\n1. Cancel all own resting orders on that instrument.\n2. Wait for own cancel-ack(s) before doing anything else on that instrument (see \u00a76 \u2014 avoids self-fills).\n3. Reset that instrument's burst-tracking state (\u00a75) and mark it \"awaiting LP burst.\"\n\n## 5. Burst-completion detection\n\nPer instrument, track LP-only state (filtered strictly by the LP's known sender ID \u2014 never the aggregate BBO feed, to avoid taker-order contamination):\n\n```\nstruct LpBurstState {\n    bool  active;\n    Price best_bid, best_ask;\n    bool  seen_bid, seen_ask;\n    Time  last_msg_time;\n};\n```\n\n- **On LP Cancel/CancelAll** (this instrument): reset `seen_bid`/`seen_ask` to false, set `active = true`, stamp `last_msg_time`.\n- **On LP Add** (this instrument): update `best_bid`/`best_ask` from that message, set the corresponding `seen_bid`/`seen_ask` flag, stamp `last_msg_time`.\n- **Completion check** (run cheaply on every incoming message, not on a timer): if `active` and `now - last_msg_time > debounce_window` and both `seen_bid` and `seen_ask` are true \u2192 burst is complete. Compute `c = mid(best_bid, best_ask)`, set `active = false`.\n\n**Debounce window:** inferred empirically from captured historical burst data \u2014 measure inter-arrival time between consecutive Add messages *within* a burst vs. the gap *before* the next burst starts. Set the window comfortably above typical intra-burst spacing and comfortably below typical inter-burst spacing. Can be refined online per-LP as more bursts are observed.\n\n**Why filter by LP sender ID only:** a taker order can transiently rest during the LP's cancel\u2192repost gap (its \"marketable\" price may not actually cross anything if the book is briefly empty). Filtering strictly to the LP's own Add messages means this never contaminates the computed `c`.\n\n## 6. Own-order sequencing (avoid self-fills)\n\nCancel-then-post must be strictly ordered per instrument to avoid crossing your own resting orders (has happened before):\n\n1. Reprice trigger fires \u2192 cancel own resting orders on this instrument.\n2. Enter `awaiting_own_cancel_ack` state for this instrument \u2014 no new orders submitted while in this state.\n3. Once cancel-ack(s) received \u2192 clear `awaiting_own_cancel_ack`, transition to `awaiting_lp_burst`.\n4. LP burst completes (\u00a75) \u2192 compute `c`, determine crossing price/side, submit new order.\n\nThis state is separate from `LpBurstState.active` \u2014 both must be clear before submitting a new order.\n\n## 7. Crossing logic\n\nOnce `c` is known (fresh, post-burst):\n- Determine crossing side and price from the LP's actual posted best bid/ask (not derived arithmetic \u2014 read the real numbers).\n- Check the live top-of-book at submission time, not just the LP-filtered view, since a taker order may be sitting at or ahead of the LP's price and will affect fill size/priority. This is fill risk to accept, not something to engineer around.\n- Submit sized to the LP's known per-level volume for that price level where knowable, otherwise a conservative default.\n\n## 8. Concurrency model\n\n- Single thread, strict in-order message processing.\n- No mutexes, no worker thread, no polling/timer thread.\n- Burst-completion check piggybacks on the normal message loop (cheap comparison run per incoming message) rather than a separate timer thread.\n- Distinguish explicitly between:\n  - **Software concurrency races** \u2014 eliminated by the single-threaded design.\n  - **Market races** (taker beating you to a fill, book state changing between observation and action) \u2014 real, unavoidable, accepted as risk rather than \"fixed.\"\n\n## 9. Secondary use of learned LP parameters\n\nOffset/levels per LP, learned from historical observation, are kept as an optional **confidence/sanity check** on burst completion (e.g. \"did we see the expected number of levels post\") \u2014 not a requirement. `c` no longer depends on them.\n\n## 10. Open items (not yet resolved)\n\n- **Fallback plan if the many-piggyback-to-one-driver clustering assumption doesn't hold** at grading time \u2014 no design yet; pinned for later.\n- Exact sizing rule when crossing (beyond \"LP's per-level volume as a starting point\").\n- Interaction with the hedger's DESK_STATE coordination signal \u2014 not revisited since the rel-recovery pivot; may need updating since `c` is now sourced differently.\n"

Order-entry request/reply is a blocking call\\n//   made from that same single thread; it stalls message processing for\\n//   the round trip, which is added latency (a market race, not a software\\n//   one), not a correctness problem -- see the ingress queue backlog note\\n//   at the top of mainLoop().\\n//\\n// ============================================================================\\n// Discovery is a one-time phase, not a loop (per explicit instruction):\\n// ============================================================================\\n//   The old design re-ran clustering every N seconds forever, with\\n//   incremental locking as clusters/drivers stabilized. That loop also\\n//   carried the (now-abandoned) rel-recovery reset logic. This version\\n//   treats discovery as two sequential, one-shot steps run once during a\\n//   warmup window before quoting starts at all:\\n//     Phase A: absorb raw market data for kWarmupDuration, building each\\n//              instrument's mid history (for driver/piggyback clustering)\\n//              and, per piggyback, a symmetry-scored history of completed\\n//              cancel/add \\\"burst\\\" episodes per sender (to find each\\n//              piggyback's LP -- see below).\\n//     Phase B: run pairwise lagged-correlation clustering once (reused\\n//              math from the previous iteration -- it was never the buggy\\n//              part) to find each cluster of related instruments; within a\\n//              cluster, the driver is the member whose trades are\\n//              concentrated in one dominant sender (the \\\"mover\\\" bot trades\\n//              its own instrument, per memories.md) -- also reused as-is\\n//              from the previous iteration's \\u00a72.4, just evaluated once\\n//              instead of re-checked every pass; then, per piggyback, pick\\n//              the sender whose completed cancel/add bursts were symmetric\\n//              about round(fv(driver)) most often as that piggyback's LP.\\n//   After Phase B, discovery never runs again -- no re-clustering, no\\n//   re-identifying the LP. The defining shape,\\n//   given directly:\\n//\\n//     CANCELS -> ADDS, and once an ADD has been seen, a CANCEL is not\\n//     allowed to extend the episode -- it starts a new one instead.\\n//\\n//         C C A A         valid (one episode)\\n//         C C C A A       valid\\n//         C C A A A       valid\\n//         C C A C A       invalid -- the second C after an A means this\\n//                          is two episodes, not one atomic requote\\n//         C A C A         invalid, same reason\\n//\\n//   BurstState below is exactly this state machine, tracked per\\n//   (instrument, sender).                 "text": "That's a classic Docker build-cache/context issue, not a save/editor problem. A few likely culprits, in order of how often I've seen each bite people:\n\n1. **Wrong build context** \u2014 your `docker-compose.yml`'s `strategy` service might point its `context`/`dockerfile` at a path that isn't actually where you're editing. If there's a stray copy of `quoter.cpp` (or the whole `strategy/` dir) elsewhere \u2014 e.g. from when you copied things around for the C++ skeleton \u2014 Docker could be faithfully rebuilding a *different* file every time.\n2. **`.dockerignore` excluding your source** \u2014 if `strategy/.dockerignore` (or a top-level one) has a pattern that matches `*.cpp` or the specific file, Docker silently won't send it in the build context, and the `COPY` in your Dockerfile picks up nothing new \u2014 but doesn't error, it just doesn't update.\n3. **A `COPY` from a cached intermediate stage** \u2014 if your Dockerfile does a multi-stage build and an early `COPY . .` layer is still cached from before `--no-cache` (unlikely with `--no-cache`, but worth ruling out if you're building via `docker compose build` and it's somehow not passing no-cache through to a stage).\n4. **Bind mount masking the built binary at runtime** \u2014 this is the one I'd bet on first: if your `docker-compose.yml` bind-mounts a host directory over `/app` (or wherever the binary lives) at *runtime*, then even a perfectly fresh build gets its output overwritten the instant the container starts, by whatever's sitting in that host folder \u2014 e.g. yesterday's compiled binary.\n\nFastest way to isolate it \u2014 run this and paste the output:\n\n```\ndocker compose build --no-cache strategy 2>&1 | tail -40\n```\n\nI want to see the actual `COPY`/build log lines \u2014 specifically whether it shows your file being copied and recompiled, or whether it's suspiciously fast (cache hit despite `--no-cache`, or copying 0 bytes changed).                         "extracted_content": "# Exchange protocol v2.5\n\nThe exchange speaks **space-separated ASCII messages over NATS**. Fields never\ncontain spaces. There are three things to talk to:\n\n| What                 | NATS subject              | Mechanism            |\n|----------------------|---------------------------|----------------------|\n| Order entry          | `ex.req.<SENDER>`         | request / reply      |\n| Market data          | `ex.md.<FEED>.<SENDER>`   | publish (JetStream)  |\n| Best bid/offer       | `ex.bbo.<FEED>`           | publish (JetStream)  |\n| Instrument metadata  | KV bucket `EX_META`       | JetStream KV         |\n\n- A **`<FEED>`** (feedcode) is 4 chars: 2 for the underlying + 2 for the expiry,\n  e.g. `AAH6`. All feedcodes on the same underlying share the prefix (`AA`).\n- A **`<SENDER>`** is an 8-char identity tag you choose for your strategy.\n- An **order id** is 8 chars you choose, unique per sender. Publicly an order is\n  identified by the 17-char `sender:orderid`.\n- Prices and volumes are integers.\n\n## Order entry \u2014 `ex.req.<SENDER>` (request/reply)\n\nPublish your request to **`ex.req.<your-sender>`** (NATS request/reply; the reply\ncomes back on the inbox). The sender in the subject is what the exchange acts on,\nand it **must match** the `<SENDER>` at the start of your message \u2014 you can only\nenter and cancel orders for your own sender. Every request starts with your\n`<SENDER>` then a 1-char type.\n\n| Type | Meaning      | Fields after `<SENDER> <type>`                                   |\n|------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `A`  | add order    | `<FEED> <id:8> <B\\|S> <volume> <price> <M\\|L\\|F>`                 |\n| `C`  | cancel order | `<FEED> <id:8>`                                                  |\n| `X`  | cancel many  | `<FEED> <B\\|S\\|X> <price>`  \u2014 see below                           |\n| `Q`  | enable STP   | `<FEED>`                                                         |\n| `W`  | disable STP  | `<FEED>`                                                          |\n\nOrder types: **`L`** = limit (rests on the book), **`M`** = market, **`F`** =\nfill-and-kill (executes what it can immediately, cancels the rest). Only `L`\nrests.\n\n**Replies** start with the exchange's tag, then:\n- `Y <n>` \u2014 accepted. For `A`, `<n>` is the volume that traded immediately. For\n  `C`/`X`, `<n>` is how many orders were cancelled.\n- `N <code> <text>` \u2014 rejected.\n\nReject codes are stable numbers with a short text. A few you will hit early:\n`100` malformed \u00b7 `202` bad feedcode \u00b7 `203` re-used order id. The rest are\nyours to catalogue by experiment.\n\n### `X` \u2014 cancel many\n\n`X <FEED> <B|S|X> <price>` cancels several of **your** resting orders at once and\nreplies `Y <n>` with the number cancelled. The `<FEED>` may also select more than\none expiry, price may select more than one price\n\n## Market data \u2014 `ex.md.<FEED>.<SENDER>`\n\nSubscribe to `ex.md.<FEED>.*` to see all market data for a contract, or to\n`ex.md.<FEED>.<your-sender>` for just your own. Every message is prefixed with an\n`int64` nanosecond timestamp.\n\n| Type | Fields after `<ts> <type>`                                          |\n|------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `A`  | `<id:17> <B\\|S> <volume> <price>`  \u2014 order added to the book          |\n| `E`  | `<incoming:17> <resting:17> <volume> <price> <matchid> <B\\|S>`        |\n| `C`  | `<id:17>`  \u2014 order removed from the book                              |\n| `T`  | same fields as `E`                                                    |\n\n- `E` is an **execution**. The trailing `B`/`S` is the **aggressor's side**. An\n  order may fill over **several** `E` messages \u2014 accumulate them.\n- `T` reports a **trade** \u2014 useful for watching trade flow.\n- Your own fills show up on `ex.md.<FEED>.<your-sender>`.\n\n## Best bid/offer \u2014 `ex.bbo.<FEED>`\n\n`<ts> <FEED> <bid_px> <bid_vol> <ask_px> <ask_vol>`, with `-` for an empty side.\nUpdated as the top of book changes.\n\n## Instrument metadata \u2014 KV `EX_META`\n\nKey = feedcode; value is `key=value` pairs: `ticksize`, `ref_price`, `band`\n(price band is `ref_price \u00b1 band`), `min_volume`, `max_volume`, `position_limit`,\n`max_tps`, `last_traded_price`. Fix identified (not yet applied): route safety-net loop through requestRequote() too, making worker thread the sole caller\n\n## Quoting-too-tight losses \u2192 pivot to wide/defensive quoting (settled)\n- Diagnosed root cause: quoting inside/near LP's ladder meant getting crossed immediately on LP reprice, refilling at a worse price \u2014 guaranteed loss each cycle\n- Confirmed via PnL CSV: a single mid-price gap of ~161 units in a ~1.3ms window explained a run of 11+ consecutive losing fills \u2014 a genuine large gap event, not routine ladder-overlap\n- Settled fix: quote one tick beyond LP's farthest ladder reach (c \u00b1 (offset+levels-1) \u00b1 1); size = LP's observed per-level volume minus 1; cancel/recalc/re-check-trigger/post-one-at-a-time/re-check-between-each-add sequence, abort-and-restart if c moves mid-post; reprice trigger = observe c itself (LP's rounding-boundary rule) independently per-piggyback\n- Jump/gap circuit breaker settled to live in the quoter (not hedger, since hedger can't cancel a still-resting stale order): per-instrument paused flag set when a jump is detected, checked at existing checkDriverFvUpdate call sites\n- Detection metric settled: track live gap |resting_px - c| continuously (not delta-between-consecutive-c-polls, since a shock's move can arrive across several smaller updates)\n\n## Rel recovery ABANDONED \u2014 pivot to new design (current, supersedes rel-recovery thread below)\n- Decided rel recovery is fundamentally unreliable (concurrency/latency-dependent, inconsistent convergence) and is being dropped entirely; reasoning: rel-based edge required winning a speed/timing race against LPs which isn't achievable, so pivoting from \"win on speed\" to \"win on price accuracy and smart quoting\"\n- New pricing approach: no longer need rel or fv(driver)+rel at all \u2014 LP's ladder is symmetric (best bid = c-offset, best ask = c+offset), so mid(best bid, best ask) read directly off the LP's own freshly-posted book equals c exactly\n- New trigger logic: round(fv(driver)) changing from previous iteration is a proxy \"reprice imminent\" flag (not exact, since it ignores rel's effect on the rounding boundary, but fires at roughly the right rate) \u2014 on trigger, immediately cancel own resting quotes on affected piggybacks and wait for the LP's fresh post\n- Profit mechanism for crossing clarified: a single fill at a fair price is ~zero-EV; the edge exists because the LP's fresh `c` reflects `fv(driver)` as of the moment it decided to reprice, not as of when the repost actually lands (driver keeps moving during the LP's multi-message repost latency) \u2014 crossing right after the fresh post exploits that lag, either via mark-to-market gain as the piggyback catches up or via having an immediate directional edge to unwind against. Condition for this to be worth anything: the driver's typical move during an LP's cancel-to-last-Add window must be large enough to beat fill/slippage risk \u2014 flagged as worth checking against captured data (expected edge per cross \u2248 typical driver movement during that latency window)\n- Burst-completion detection settled: per-instrument state (best_bid/best_ask/seen_bid/seen_ask/last_msg_time), reset on LP cancel, updated on LP Add messages (filtered by LP's own sender ID only, not aggregate BBO, to avoid taker-order contamination), considered complete when quiet for a debounce window and both sides seen; debounce window to be inferred empirically from captured historical burst inter-arrival-time data\n- Clarified threading model: nats.c itself runs internal I/O/delivery threads (can't be made literally single-threaded), so \"single-threaded\" now means only one synchronization boundary exists \u2014 NATS callback thread does a minimal enqueue only, one dedicated consumer thread (mainLoop) processes everything else (parsing, state, decisions, orders) in order; all business state (LpBurstState etc.) is touched only by that one consumer thread\n- Distinguishes market race conditions (state changing between observation and action \u2014 inherent risk, not fixable by architecture) from software concurrency races (fixed by going single-threaded) \u2014 taker orders potentially resting during an LP's cancel/repost gap and fill-priority risk when crossing are treated as the former, not bugs to engineer around\n- Open item: sequencing between own-quote cancel-ack and firing the new crossing order \u2014 considering a per-instrument \"awaiting own cancel ack\" flag to avoid double-side exposure, not yet decided/implemented\n- Decided crossing order volume will match the LP's own volume at that price level (not a fraction/minus-one adjustment like the old defensive-quoting design used)\n- Fallback plan sketch (partial, deferred for later): if piggybacks turn out unrelated to any driver, will still identify and exclude front-months from quoting entirely (considers trading them directly \"suicide\"); for unrelated back-months, considering entering the book only via mean-reversion when reversion looks imminent, rather than continuous two-sided quoting \u2014 not fully worked out, explicitly deprioritized until after the current design is built\n\n## [SUPERSEDED] Old rel-recovery debugging thread (abandoned, kept for history)\n- Symptom before abandoning: rel samples scattered wildly (121.5, 105.0, 15.5, -77.5 across consecutive samples) with sdTicks increasing (46\u219251+) as more samples accumulated \u2014 signature of a bias/mixture problem, not insufficient sample count\n- Key insight that contributed to the decision to abandon: NATS gives no cross-subscriber delivery-order/timing guarantee, so LP's fv(driver)-at-decision-time and live-read fv(driver) aren't guaranteed to agree even off the same subscription \u2014 recovering rel precisely was fighting causality itself\n\n## Process notes\n- User expressed a moment of doubt about strategic thinking ability after several rounds on the rel-recovery sub-problem\n- Pipeline now has 8+ sequential stages (discovery, debounce, burst detection, contamination guard, causal anchor, rel trust gate, concurrency-safe queue, jump detection) \u2014 worth reassessing against actual grading bar (profitable + low risk) once current debugging thread resolves\n</content>\n",

the edge exists because the LP's fresh `c` reflects `fv(driver)` as of the moment it decided to reprice, not as of when the repost actually lands (driver keeps moving during the LP's multi-message repost latency) \u2014 crossing right after the fresh post exploits that lag, either via mark-to-market gain as the piggyback catches up or via having an immediate directional edge to unwind against. Condition for this to be worth anything: the driver's typical move during an LP's cancel-to-last-Add window must be large enough to beat fill/slippage risk \u2014 flagged as worth checking against captured data (expected edge per cross \u2248 typical driver movement during that latency window)\n- Burst-completion detection settled: per-instrument state (best_bid/best_ask/seen_bid/seen_ask/last_msg_time), reset on LP cancel, updated on LP Add messages (filtered by LP's own sender ID only, not aggregate BBO, to avoid taker-order contamination), considered complete when quiet for a debounce window and both sides seen; all business state (LpBurstState etc.) is touched only by that one consumer thread\n- Distinguishes market race conditions (state changing between observation and action \u2014 inherent risk, not fixable by architecture) from software concurrency races (fixed by going single-threaded) \u2014 taker orders potentially resting during an LP's cancel/repost gap and fill-priority risk when crossing are treated as the former, not bugs to engineer around\n- Open item: sequencing between own-quote cancel-ack and firing the new crossing order \u2014 considering a per-instrument \"awaiting own cancel ack\" flag to avoid double-side exposure, not yet decided/implemented\n- Decided crossing order volume will match the LP's own volume at that price level (not a fraction/minus-one adjustment like the old defensive-quoting design used)\n- Fallback plan sketch (partial, deferred for later): if piggybacks turn out unrelated to any driver, will still identify and exclude front-months from quoting entirely (considers trading them directly \"suicide\"); The LP with the largest offset has a wider spread, meaning their ask is even higher and their bid is even lower \u2014 worse for you on both sides, not better. There's no LP pair where one's ask is below another's bid. So there's no arbitrage across LPs on the same instrument, ever, by construction. It's the more standard/robust of the two (handles the fallback edge cases), it's what the rest of the system's math is defined in terms of, and it'll match simple mid closely enough in practice that you're not losing anything by standardizing on it.\n\n**How much to quote (sizing)**\n\nThis needs a few ingredients you already have, plus a decision on strategy shape:\n\n1. **Known worst case, for free.** Since `target` is clipped to `[440, 760]` around a mean of 600, the maximum possible deviation from mean is exactly 160. So: size = f(|current_price \u2212 600 (or 600+rel)|), increasing with the deviation, similar to how a classic mean-reversion market maker scales into a position more aggressively the further price is from fair value, and scales down/flattens near the mean.\n3. **Cap by position limits and margin**, not just by conviction \u2014 you have `position_limit` in EX_META and your own `$100k` margin bound; size should never let a full-adverse move against your position blow through those.\n4. **Watch out for LP-level sizing precedent** \u2014 your earlier defensive-quoting design used \"LP's observed per-level volume minus 1\" as a heuristic for how much size is safe to rest without excessive adverse-selection risk; that's a separate, useful constraint that still applies even in a mean-reversion-driven design, since it caps how much you're exposed on a single ladder level regardless of your directional conviction.\n\nDo you want to work out an actual sizing formula (e.g. linear in deviation, capped at some fraction of position_limit) now, or first pin down the reversion half-life so you know what holding-period risk you're sizing against?",

Let's build it up conceptually first, then you write it.\n\n**The core mental model**\n\nNATS C client (nats.c) is fundamentally callback-driven, not a simple blocking read loop like you might expect. This matters a lot for your architecture, since your quoter is built around \"one dedicated consumer thread processes everything in order.\" The library's own I/O thread invokes your callback whenever a message arrives \u2014 your callback does NOT run on the thread you called `natsConnection_Subscribe` from. So the first design question is:\n\n**Q1:** Given that NATS delivers messages to you via a callback from its own internal thread, and your design has a single `mainLoop` consumer thread that must own all business state \u2014 what does your subscription callback need to do (and *not* do) to keep that invariant?\n\nThink about that before reading on \u2014 it's the same shape of problem as your earlier concurrency fixes in quoter.cpp (enqueue-only in the callback, real work in mainLoop).\n\n**The four building blocks you actually need**\n\n1. **Connect** \u2014 `natsConnection_Connect(&conn, opts)` or the simpler `natsConnection_ConnectTo(&conn, url)`. Gets you a `natsConnection*`.\n2. **Subscribe** \u2014 `natsConnection_Subscribe(&sub, conn, subject, callback, closure)`. The `closure` pointer is how you pass your queue/context into the callback without globals.\n3. **Publish** \u2014 `natsConnection_PublishString` / `natsConnection_Publish` for raw bytes \u2014 this is how you send orders (Add/Cancel per PROTOCOL.md).\n4. **KV access** \u2014 since EX_META and DESK_STATE are KV buckets, you need `natsConnection_JetStream` \u2192 `js_KeyValue_...` calls (different code path from plain pub/sub \u2014 this is probably the part you actually haven't built from scratch yet, even though you've *read* EX_META before).\n\n**Q2:** You already know your callback needs to be a fast enqueue.                 "text": "That analogy actually works really well \u2014 let me sharpen the one place it's slightly off.\n\n**Where it's exactly right:** yes, pub/sub is \"fire and forget past a moment in time\" \u2014 if nobody's subscribed *right when* a message goes out, it's gone (like a Reel/story that's live-then-gone if you're not watching). KV is persistent, current-state storage you can read whenever you want, regardless of when it was written \u2014 much more DM-like in the sense that the content just sits there waiting for you.\n\n**Where it's subtly different from a DM:** a DM is usually thought of as an accumulating history \u2014 every message stays, you scroll back through all of them. KV is the opposite of that: **each key holds exactly one current value** \u2014 writing a new value *overwrites* the old one, you don't get a log of every past value by default (unless you specifically go looking at KV history/revisions, which is a separate feature). So it's less \"DM thread\" and more like... a shared whiteboard/label on a box: whoever looks at the \"AAH6\" label right now sees whatever was most recently written there, and earlier writes are gone unless someone explicitly kept a history.\n\nThat distinction is actually important for `DESK_STATE`: if your hedger writes an urgency value, then writes a new one 200ms later, the quoter reading it just sees the latest \u2014 it can't tell \"how urgency has evolved,\" only \"what's true right now.\" Good enough for your coordination design since it's about current state (\"should I be defensive right now\"), not history \u2014 but worth knowing it's a fundamentally different guarantee from pub/sub, not just \"pub/sub with persistence added.\"\n\n**Now your own question back to you, since you got the \"why\" mostly right already:** given EX_META is written once when the exchange starts up and basically never changes after that (ticksize, band, etc. are static per instrument) \u2014 does the \"current value only, no history\" nature of KV cost you anything for EX_META specifically, the way it might for DESK_STATE?",

Fix identified (not yet applied): route safety-net loop through requestRequote() too, making worker thread the sole caller\n\n## Quoting-too-tight losses \u2192 pivot to wide/defensive quoting (settled)\n- Diagnosed root cause: quoting inside/near LP's ladder meant getting crossed immediately on LP reprice, refilling at a worse price \u2014 guaranteed loss each cycle\n- Confirmed via PnL CSV: a single mid-price gap of ~161 units in a ~1.3ms window explained a run of 11+ consecutive losing fills \u2014 a genuine large gap event, not routine ladder-overlap\n- Settled fix: quote one tick beyond LP's farthest ladder reach (c \u00b1 (offset+levels-1) \u00b1 1); reasoning: rel-based edge required winning a speed/timing race against LPs which isn't achievable, so pivoting from \"win on speed\" to \"win on price accuracy and smart quoting\"\n- New pricing approach: no longer need rel or fv(driver)+rel at all \u2014 LP's ladder is symmetric (best bid = c-offset, best ask = c+offset), so mid(best bid, best ask) read directly off the LP's own freshly-posted book equals c exactly\n- New trigger logic: round(fv(driver)) changing from previous iteration is a proxy \"reprice imminent\" flag (not exact, since it ignores rel's effect on the rounding boundary, but fires at roughly the right rate) \u2014 on trigger, immediately cancel own resting quotes on affected piggybacks and wait for the LP's fresh post\n- Profit mechanism for crossing clarified: a single fill at a fair price is ~zero-EV; the edge exists because the LP's fresh `c` reflects `fv(driver)` as of the moment it decided to reprice, not as of when the repost actually lands (driver keeps moving during the LP's multi-message repost latency) \u2014 crossing right after the fresh post exploits that lag, either via mark-to-market gain as the piggyback catches up or via having an immediate directional edge to unwind against. Condition for this to be worth anything: the driver's typical move during an LP's cancel-to-last-Add window must be large enough to beat fill/slippage risk \u2014 flagged as worth checking against captured data (expected edge per cross \u2248 typical driver movement during that latency window)\n- Burst-completion detection settled: per-instrument state (best_bid/best_ask/seen_bid/seen_ask/last_msg_time), reset on LP cancel, updated on LP Add messages (filtered by LP's own sender ID only, not aggregate BBO, to avoid taker-order contamination), considered complete when quiet for a debounce window and both sides seen; all business state (LpBurstState etc.) is touched only by that one consumer thread\n- Distinguishes market race conditions (state changing between observation and action \u2014 inherent risk, not fixable by architecture) from software concurrency races (fixed by going single-threaded) \u2014 taker orders potentially resting during an LP's cancel/repost gap and fill-priority risk when crossing are treated as the former, not bugs to engineer around\n- Open item: sequencing between own-quote cancel-ack and firing the new crossing order \u2014 considering a per-instrument \"awaiting own cancel ack\" flag to avoid double-side exposure, not yet decided/implemented\n- Decided crossing order volume will match the LP's own volume at that price level (not a fraction/minus-one adjustment like the old defensive-quoting design used)\n- Fallback plan sketch (partial, deferred for later): if piggybacks turn out unrelated to any driver, will still identify and exclude front-months from quoting entirely (considers trading them directly \"suicide\");
